It covers non-equilibrium situations where the forces are not of gradient type and the invariant measure does not have an explicit density, extending previous results set in the equilibrium case. The key argument is to establish the hypercontractivity of the associated semigroup, which follows from its hyperboundedness and its $L^2$-exponential ergodicity. Moreover, we obtain exponential ergodicity in the $L^2$-Wasserstein distance by combining Talagrand's inequality with a log-Harnack inequality. These results are further extended to the McKean-Vlasov setting and to the associated mean-field interacting particle systems under a suitable smallness condition on the distribution dependence. In the latter case, the convergence rates are uniform in the number of particles and we also establish the hypercontractivity and log-Sobolev inequality uniform in the number of particles using a new approach based on Girsanov's transform and hypercontractivity.

papers.title: A nonsmooth extension of the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem via metric regularity techniques and applications to nonlinear PDEs
papers.abstract: We generalize the Brezzi-Rappaz-Raviart approximation theorem, which allows to obtain existence and a priori error estimates for approximations of solutions to some nonlinear partial differential equations. Our contribution lies in the fact that we typically allow for nonlinearities having merely Lipschitz regularity, while previous results required some form of differentiability. This is achieved by making use of the theory of metrically regular mappings, developed in the context of variational analysis. We apply this generalization to derive quasi-optimal error estimates for finite element approximations to solutions of viscous Hamilton-Jacobi equations and second order mean field game systems.

papers.title: Salvetti complexes for conditional oriented matroids
papers.abstract: We give a new proof of the fact that the complement of the complexification of a real hyperplane arrangement is homotopy equivalent to the Salvetti complex of the associated oriented matroid. Our proof involves no choices, is relatively easy to visualize, and generalizes to the setting of conditional oriented matroids.
papers.comments: Fixed typos and updated references. Version to appear in Advances in Applied Mathematics

papers.title: Embedding lattices of quasivarieties of periodic groups into lattices of additively idempotent semiring varieties: An algebraic proof
papers.abstract: A general result by Jackson (Flat algebras and the translation of universal Horn logic to equational logic, J. Symb. Log. 73(1) (2008) 90--128) implies that the lattice of all quasivarieties of groups of exponent dividing $n$ embeds into the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$ of all varieties of additively idempotent semirings whose multiplicative semigroups are unions of groups of exponent dividing $n$; the image of this embedding is an interval in $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$. We provide a new, direct, and purely algebraic proof of these facts and present a new identity basis for the top variety of the interval. In addition, we obtain new information about the lattice $L(\mathbf{Sr}_n)$, demonstrating that the properties of the lattice for $n\ge 3$ differ drastically from those previously known when $n=1$ or $2$.
papers.comments: 21 pages, 2 figures. In version 3, an error in the proof of Theorem 5.2 has been fixed

papers.title: Abstract Formulation of Mean-Field Models and Propagation of Chaos
papers.abstract: We formulate a unified abstract framework for mean-field particle systems and their macroscopic limits from the perspective of differential equations and functional analysis. Combining semigroup theory with optimal transport, we study measure-valued evolutions directly through their generators, allowing different classes of mean-field models to be treated within a common structure. Specifically, the framework involves (1) formulating mean-field models abstractly using semigroups and generators; (2) establishing well-posedness of the corresponding nonlinear mean-field evolution equations in a class of solutions stable under approximation; and (3) proving quantitative propagation of chaos for the associated $N$-particle systems. The central tool is the transport derivative, which measures the infinitesimal variation of transport costs between Markov evolutions. We establish transport-stability criteria expressed through local generator inequalities and show how these criteria underpin both nonlinear well-posedness and particle approximation. When the generator's dependence on the law is controlled by averaged Hilbert-valued features, we obtain an $O(N^{-1})$ sampling contribution to the quadratic Wasserstein estimate through a variance argument. As an application, we obtain quantitative propagation of chaos for Lévy-type mean-field systems with state- and law-dependent drift, diffusion, and jump kernels under intrinsic transport conditions. The admissible jump kernels extend beyond those generated by multiplicative Lévy noise, demonstrating the scope of the abstract framework.

papers.title: Unimodality and Cluster Algebras from Surfaces
papers.abstract: We prove that the rank polynomial of the lattice of order ideals of a loop fence poset is unimodal. This poset arises as the poset of join-irreducibles in the lattice of good matchings of loop graphs associated with notched arcs. Equivalently, such polynomials can be obtained by evaluating all coefficient variables in an F-polynomial at a single variable q. We also conclude that the rank polynomial of any tagged arc, whether plain or notched, is not only unimodal but also satisfies a symmetry condition known as almost interlacing. Furthermore, when the lamination consists of a single curve, the cluster expansion-evaluated by setting all cluster variables to 1 and all coefficient variables to q-is also unimodal. We conjecture that polynomials in this case are log-concave.

papers.title: A marking graph for finite-type Artin groups
papers.abstract: Clean markings on surfaces were a key component in Masur and Minsky's hierarchy machinery, which proved to be a powerful tool in the study of mapping class groups. We construct a marking graph for irreducible finite-type Artin groups which is quasi-isometric to the group modulo its center, i.e., an element of $A_Γ/Z(A_Γ)$ is determined up to finite error by its action on one of our markings. To construct this graph, we construct suitable collections of transverse parabolic subgroups which extend the maximal simplices of the complex of irreducible parabolic subgroups to analogues of clean markings, and we define natural analogues of elementary moves.
papers.comments: 58 pages. v2: minor corrections and improvements v3: version accepted to Journal of the London Mathematical Society

papers.title: Statistical stability for systems semi-conjugate to pre-piecewise \textit{convex or expanding} maps with countably many branches
papers.abstract: We investigate the statistical stability of a class of dynamical systems semi-conjugate to pre-piecewise \textit{convex or expanding} maps with countably many branches. These systems naturally arise in the study of transformations with unbounded derivatives, discontinuities, or infinite Markov partitions; features that pose significant challenges for stability analysis. Specifically, we consider one-parameter families of transformations $\{F_δ\}_{δ\in [0,1)}$ and their corresponding invariant measures $\{μ_δ\}$. We provide general conditions ensuring that the unperturbed measure $μ_0$ is statistically stable, meaning the map $δ\mapsto μ_δ$ is continuous at $δ= 0$ in the appropriate topology. Furthermore, we establish explicit quantitative estimates for the modulus of continuity of $μ_δ$ in terms of the perturbation parameter $δ$. Our results apply to a broad class of maps, including those semi-conjugate to classical examples such as the Gauss and Lüroth maps.
papers.comments: This is the final version of this manuscript

papers.title: Exploration of vertical self-resonant bifurcations from Distant Retrograde Orbits (DROs) in the Earth-Moon Circular Restricted Three-Body Problem (CR3BP)
papers.abstract: This paper investigates vertical self-resonant bifurcations from the Distant Retrograde Orbit (DRO) family in the Earth-Moon circular restricted three-body problem. Using a predictor-corrector continuation algorithm, we identify fourteen vertical-critical DROs consisting of twelve higher-order periods of multiplicity from integer multiples of five to ten and two vertical pitchfork bifurcations. Their continuation generates twenty-five families of spatial symmetric periodic orbits. Beyond the computation of new periodic orbit families, the main contribution of this work is a systematic characterization of the resulting global bifurcation topology through symplectic invariants. To this end, we combine Floquet multiplier transitions at local bifurcations with Conley-Zehnder indices, Krein signatures and the Euler characteristic of the local Floer homology to develop a computational symplectic framework that systematically classifies the bifurcated families and provides a topological interpretation of their numerically established connections. The computations reveal a global bifurcation network generated by the DRO family, including bridge families that connect the DROs with Butterfly, planar prograde and P3DRO families, together with several families consisting of long-period multi-excursion orbits that approach collision with the Moon. The computations also identify spatial periodic orbits satisfying Earth-Moon resonances along several bifurcated families.

papers.title: A case of the dijoin conjecture on inverting oriented graphs
papers.abstract: For an oriented graph $D$, the inversion of $X\subseteq V(D)$ in $D$ is the graph obtained by reversing the orientation of all arcs with both ends in $X$. The inversion number $\mathrm{inv}(D)$ is the minimum number of inversions needed to obtain an acyclic oriented graph. We show that the dijoin conjecture of Bang-Jensen, da Silva and Havet, that $\mathrm{inv}(D_1\rightarrow D_2)=\mathrm{inv}(D_1)+\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$, is true in the case where $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ is even. We also characterise the cases $\mathrm{inv}(D_1)=2$ and $\mathrm{inv}(D_2)$ odd, for which the conjecture does and does not hold. We then go on to show a similar result for n-joins, in doing so we prove a conjecture of Alon, Powierski, Savery, Scott and Wilmer. Our proofs build on the idea of tournament minimum rank, introduced by Behague, Johnston, Morrison and Ogden.
papers.comments: 16 pages. Version 2: minor edits and clarifications

papers.title: Property B: A Baumgartner-style Property that Applies to Preservation of $\aleph_1$ and $\aleph_2$ under Iterations with Supports of Size $\aleph_1$
papers.abstract: We prove a theorem on iterated forcing that can be used for preservation of $\aleph_2$ and $\aleph_1$ in the usual iterations along an ordinal, with supports of size $\aleph_1$ of forcings that have amalgamation properties similar to those present in the perfect set forcing. The work is modelled after Baumgartner's Axiom A and his proof that iterations with countable support of the same preserve $\aleph_1$. In honour of James E. Baumgartner, the property introduced here is called Property B$(κ)$. The known additional difficulties when forcing at cardinals higher than $\aleph_1$ make for a less general theorem and a more complex theorem on the iteration, which is not an iteration theorem in the classical sense. The results extend to other cardinals $κ$ such that $κ^{<κ}=κ$, in place of $\aleph_1$. We give examples of individual forcings that have Property B$(κ)$ and their products. In particular, we introduce a correct version of the generalised perfect set forcing, which we call Perfect Set Forcing with Respect to a Filter. We give its basic properties and show that for the right kind of filter $\mathcal F$ this kind of forcing is iterable with supports of size $\leκ$. Our further work has extended some of the results from the paper to iterations along any well-founded partial order.
papers.comments: The version answering the comments of a referee

papers.title: A FISTA-type Riemannian Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method
papers.abstract: We study accelerated proximal gradient methods for minimizing the sum of a smooth and a nonsmooth function on Riemannian manifolds. Accelerated convergence rates under geodesic convexity have not been established for some existing methods, and global geodesic convexity may fail or be difficult to verify. We develop a Riemannian accelerated proximal gradient method that combines tangent-space proximal steps with momentum updates based on parallel transport and the exponential map. Under geodesic $μ$-strong convexity ($μ\geqslant0$) of the smooth term and pullback $ρ$-convexity ($ρ\in\mathbb{R}$) of the nonsmooth term, we establish accelerated convergence rates for the objective gap: an $\mathcal{O}(k^{-2})$ rate when $μ-ρ\geqslant0$ and a linear rate when $μ-ρ>0$, where $k$ is the iteration count. The rates depend on sectional curvature bounds and the diameter of a prescribed region assumed to contain the iterates. For nonconvex objectives or unknown problem parameters, we further consider an adaptive restart variant with proximal gradient safeguards. If the initial sublevel set is compact, we prove that every accumulation point of the safeguard reference sequence is stationary and that an $\varepsilon$-stationary point is obtained within $\mathcal{O}(\varepsilon^{-2})$ iterations for any tolerance $\varepsilon>0$. Both methods also apply to smooth objectives. In this setting, the basic method yields a single Riemannian accelerated gradient scheme for geodesically convex and geodesically $μ$-strongly convex problems. Its iteration and parameter recurrence extend continuously to $μ=0$, and a single analysis establishes accelerated rates in both cases. Numerical experiments on nonsmooth composite and smooth problems demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.
papers.comments: v1 to v2: Updated title and abstract, restructured manuscript, revised theoretical analysis, and redesigned numerical experiments. Thanks to all who provided valuable comments and suggestions on this work

papers.title: $m$-Positivity and Regularisation
papers.abstract: Starting from the notion of $m$-plurisubharmonic function introduced recently by Dieu and studied, in particular, by Harvey and Lawson, we consider $m$-(semi-)positive $(1,\,1)$-currents and Hermitian holomorphic line bundles on complex Hermitian manifolds and prove two kinds of results: vanishing theorems and $L^2$-estimates for the $\bar\partial$-equation in the context of $C^\infty$ $m$-positive Hermitian fibre metrics; global and local regularisation theorems for $m$-semi-positive $(1,\,1)$-currents whose proofs involve the use of viscosity subsolutions for a certain Monge-Ampère-type equation and the associated Dirichlet problem. The results of the latter type require techniques of a substantially different nature from those of the classical $m=1$ case and have already been applied in subsequent joint work of the present authors and in further work of the second-named author with K. Broder.
papers.comments: 38 pages; to appear in Mathematische Zeitschrift

papers.title: A convenient category of locales
papers.abstract: The notion of Kan extendable subcategories was initially introduced to define the category of compactly generated fibrewise topological spaces over a T1 base space and to establish its cartesian closure. In this paper, we show that the same framework can likewise be applied to define the category of compactly generated strongly Hausdorff locales and to prove that it, too, is cartesian closed
papers.journal_ref: Appl. Categ. Structures 34 (2026), no. 6, Paper No. 66

papers.title: Adjusting SPRT for an Asymptotically Efficient Procedure with Finite Number of Applications of Less Effective Treatment
papers.abstract: We propose an adaptive Sequential Probability Ratio Test (SPRT) with a finite expected number of allocations to the less effective treatment. In the classical SPRT framework, patients are assigned to the two competing treatments one-by-one until a stopping criterion, based on breaching the boundary values which are pre-determined using the Type-I and Type-II error probabilities, is met. This controls the errors at the cost of ethical efficiency as the exposure to the less effective treatment is large. For testing two simple hypotheses, our proposed procedure employs a likelihood ratio-driven adaptive allocation rule, dynamically concentrating sampling effort on the superior population while preserving asymptotic efficiency (in terms of average sample number) comparable to the classical SPRT. We show that at each step, the allocated observations remain independent despite the data-dependent allocation, prove that the expected number of allocations to the inferior treatment remains finite, with an explicit upper bound, and derive a closed-form approximation to it. Extensive simulation studies and data-calibrated case studies substantiate the theoretical results, evincing a significant reduction in inferior allocations compared to the classical SPRT. The proposed design thus offers a balanced method between statistical precision and ethical responsibility, aligning inferential reliability with patient safety.

papers.title: Equi-integrable approximation of Sobolev mappings between manifolds
papers.abstract: We show that limits of sequences of smooth maps between compact Riemannian manifolds with equi-integrable $W^{1, p}$-Sobolev energy can always be strongly approximated by smooth maps, giving a counterpart of Hang's density result in $W^{1, 1}$ for the Sobolev space $W^{1, p}$ with integer $p \ge 2$. Our result extends to higher-order Sobolev spaces and is straightforward in fractional Sobolev spaces. We also provide a proof based on the weak continuity of Jacobians in the cases where the cohomological criterion of Bethuel, Demengel, Colon and Hélein applies.

papers.title: Variational analysis of determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: Determinantal varieties---the sets of bounded-rank matrices or tensors---have attracted growing interest in low-rank optimization. The tangent cone to low-rank sets is widely studied and underpins a range of geometric methods. The second-order geometry, which encodes curvature information, is more intricate. In this work, we develop a unified framework to derive explicit formulas for both first- and second-order tangent sets to various low-rank sets, including low-rank matrices, tensors, symmetric matrices, and positive semidefinite matrices. The framework also accommodates the intersection of a low-rank set and another set satisfying some assumptions, thereby yielding a tangent intersection rule. Through the lens of tangent sets, we establish a necessary and sufficient condition under which a nonsmooth problem and its smooth parameterization share equivalent second-order stationary points. As applications, we exploit tangent sets to characterize optimality conditions for low-rank optimization and prove that verifying second-order optimality is NP-hard. Moreover, for low-rank semidefinite programs, the Burer--Monteiro parameterization maps fourth-order stationary points of the parameterized problem to second-order stationary points of the original problem. In a separate line of analysis, we investigate variational geometry of the graph of the normal cone to matrix varieties, deriving the explicit Bouligand tangent cone, Fréchet and Mordukhovich normal cones to the graph. These results are further applied to develop optimality conditions for low-rank bilevel programs.

papers.title: Linear independence of values of Dirichlet $L$ functions
papers.abstract: For any Dirichlet character $χ$ with conductor $N$, we give a lower bound of order $\sqrt{s/\log(s)}$ on the dimension of the $\mathbb{Q}(e^{2iπ/\varphi(N)})$-vector space spanned by the values of its $L$-function at integers $2\leq i\leq s$ of the parity opposite to that of $χ$, where $\varphi$ is Euler's totient function. This generalizes a 2026 result of Fischler, which corresponds to principal characters. To this end, we construct linear combinations of these values of $L$-functions using a refined version of Siegel's lemma, and apply to them a linear independence criterion that generalizes Fischler's. To verify a crucial hypothesis of this criterion, we rely on a ``Shidlovskii's lemma".

papers.title: Infinitely many positive normalized solutions for Schrödinger equations with nonlinear point defects on noncompact metric graphs
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the multiplicity of positive normalized solutions for the following Schrödinger equation with nonlinear point defects on a general metric graph $\G=(\V,\E)$, possibly with infinitely many edges \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u'' = λu & \text{on every } \e \in \E, \\ \int_\G \abs{u}^2\, dx = μ& \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = -\abs{u(\vv)}^{p-2}u(\vv) & \text{at every } \vv \in \V_0, \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = 0 & \text{at every } \vv \in \V \setminus \V_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p>2$, $\G$ is connected, $\V_0 \subset \V$ is nonempty, $μ>0$ is a given constant, $λ$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplie. For $p\neq4$, every fixed nonempty finite set $W\subset\V_0$ gives at least $2^{\#W}-1$ distinct positive normalized solutions, for every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$ and for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$. When $\V_0$ is finite and $\G$ is noncompact with the bottom of the Kirchhoff Laplacian spectrum equal to zero, we prove that there are exactly $2^{\#\V_0}-1$ positive solutions at every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$, and at every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and $|\overline B_r(o)|=O(r^{4/p})$ as $r\to+\infty$ for a fixed $o\in\G$. If infinitely many defect vertices $\vv \in \V_0$ have uniformly bounded degree, we also obtain infinitely many positive solutions that are pairwise inequivalent under the automorphisms of $\G$ preserving $\V_0$, for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $2<p<4$ and for every prescribed mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$. In the $L^2$-critical ($p=4$) case, under local conditions near the selected defect vertices, analogous results hold for masses slightly below $kq^2/2$, where $k$ is the number of these vertices and $q$ is their common degree.
papers.comments: 82 pages. Comments and suggestions are most welcome

papers.title: Computations with diagonal simplicial tensor modules
papers.abstract: For each vertex order $π$ of a finite simple graph on at least two vertices, insert an isolated vertex between successive vertices. In the resulting adjacency matrix $A$, deleting row $i$ and column $i$ gives a principal submatrix $A_i$. The alternating sum of the $A_i$ is the simplicial boundary of $A$ and has full rank over $\mathbb F_2$ exactly when $π$ traces a Hamiltonian path. Each Hamiltonian path gives two full-rank orders. We tabulate boundary rank distributions over all vertex orders of the Petersen, $4\times4$ rook, and Shrikhande graphs. Full-rank counts distinguish the cospectral rook and Shrikhande graphs. For each finite graph, vertex and edge tensors in a three-axis diagonal simplicial tensor module generate a simplicial submodule whose normalized chains form the graph's incidence complex and compute its homology. Let $X$ be a diagonal simplicial tensor module on $k\ge1$ axes over a nonzero unital commutative ring. We give coordinate bases for its horn kernels and normalized chains. A horn has a unique filler exactly when its degree exceeds $k$. For a shape in $X$ of simplicial dimension $n$ (shortest axis length $n+1$), the simplicial module $X$ is an $n$-hypergroupoid exactly when $k\le n$. We prove analogous bounds for horn filling in a dendroidal module on rooted trees. Over a field, we construct a rational map from the space of hypermatrices of fixed shape and degree to a product of Grassmannians. The reduced closure of its image is rational and, over $\mathbb C$, is isomorphic to a Schubert variety. Python code for this paper's examples and rank tables is at https://github.com/flengyel/SimplicialTensors.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 1 figure, 2 tables. Rewritten and retitled. Programs for the tensor and graph computations are available at https://github.com/flengyel/SimplicialTensors

papers.title: Affine Invariant Langevin Dynamics for rare-event sampling
papers.abstract: We introduce an affine invariant Langevin dynamics (ALDI) framework for the efficient estimation of rare events in nonlinear dynamical systems. Rare events are formulated as Bayesian inverse problems through a nonsmooth limit-state function whose zero level set characterises the event of interest. To overcome the nondifferentiability of this function, we propose a smooth approximation that preserves the failure set and yields a posterior distribution satisfying the small-noise limit. The resulting potential is sampled by ALDI, a (derivative-free) interacting particle system whose affine invariance allows it to adapt to the local anisotropy of the posterior. We demonstrate the performance of the method across a hierarchy of benchmarks, namely two low-dimensional examples (an algebraic problem with convex geometry and a dynamical problem of saddle-type instability) and a point-vortex model for atmospheric blockings. In all cases, ALDI concentrates near the relevant near-critical sets and provides accurate proposal distributions for self-normalised importance sampling. The framework is computationally robust, potentially gradient-free, and well-suited for complex forward models with strong geometric anisotropy. These results highlight ALDI as a promising tool for rare-event estimation in unstable regimes of dynamical systems.

papers.title: Variational estimates for discrete spherical averages: $\ell^p$-boundedness and related arithmetic obstructions
papers.abstract: In this article, we investigate variational inequalities for the family of discrete spherical averages. We establish $\ell^p$-boundedness of the $r$-variation operators for $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$ along sufficiently sparse sequences of factorial radii. Moreover, we also study arithmetic obstructions to these variational estimates and construct counterexamples to show that such boundedness properties for the corresponding variational operators cannot hold for lacunary sequences of radii.
papers.comments: Major revision. An error in a lemma used in the previous version was identified (originally cited from the literature). As a consequence, some earlier results do not hold as stated. The article has been rewritten using a different approach. 21 pages

papers.title: Arboreal Networks and Ultrametrics
papers.abstract: Ultrametrics are an important class of distances used in applications such as phylogenetics, clustering and classification theory. Ultrametrics are essentially distances that can be represented by an edge-weighted rooted tree so that all of the distances in the tree from the root to any leaf of the tree are equal. In this paper, we introduce a generalization of ultrametrics called arboreal ultrametrics which have applications in phylogenetics and also arise in the theory of distance-hereditary graphs. These are partial distances, that is distances that are not necessarily defined for every pair of elements in the groundset, that can be represented by an ultrametric arboreal network, that is, an edge-weighted rooted network whose underlying graph is a tree. As with ultrametrics all of the distances in the ultrametric arboreal network from any root to any leaf below it are are equal but, in contrast, the network may have more than one root. In our two main results we characterize when a partial distance is an arboreal ultrametric as well as proving that, somewhat surprisingly, given any unrooted edge-weighted phylogenetic tree there is a necessarily unique way to insert roots into this tree so as to obtain an arboreal ultrametric.

papers.title: A hierarchical splitting approach for N-split differential equations
papers.abstract: We propose a hierarchical splitting approach that constructs splitting methods for N-split differential equations by iteratively applying splitting methods for two-split systems along a splitting tree. Since assigning methods of order p to all nodes of the tree yields a hierarchical splitting method of order p, the order theory for two-split systems carries over to any number of partitions. We derive explicit formulas for the leading-order error terms, investigate self-adjointness, and show that state-of-the-art composition approaches are contained in the resulting class as special cases. Augmenting the approach with multiple time stepping yields a framework at the intersection of geometric numerical integration and multirate integration, for which we characterize the computational order of a multirate integrator and introduce a reweighting of the multirate factors that reduces computational overhead, but can lead to an order reduction when applied within composition techniques. We further discuss principles for designing splitting trees, with particular attention to separable Hamiltonian systems and port-Hamiltonian systems. Numerical experiments for both classes demonstrate that the hierarchical splitting approach yields efficient methods for N-split systems. We find that the approach is particularly efficient when commutator-based splitting methods become available and the partitions evolve on distinct time scales.

papers.title: Composition operators on weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc
papers.abstract: We study composition operators between weighted Bergman spaces of the polydisc induced by smooth symbols. We prove a general result of continuity which only involves the behaviour of the symbol on the polytorus. We deduce from this several consequences about the automatic continuity of the induced operator. We study in depth the case of the tridisc and exhibit several examples showing that a characterization of continuity using only derivatives seems impossible.

papers.title: On the Damped Euler-Monge-Ampere equations with Radial Symmetry: Critical Thresholds and Large-Time Behavior
papers.abstract: We investigate the global well-posedness and large-time dynamics of the pressureless Euler-Monge-Ampere (EMA) system with velocity damping in multidimensions, subject to radially symmetric initial data. We first establish the phenomenon of critical thresholds, where subcritical initial data maintain global regularity, and supercritical initial data lead to finite time singularity formation. We provide two methods for constructing these thresholds: a refined spectral dynamics approach based on Liu and Tadmor (2002 Commun. Math. Phy. 228 435-66) and a comparison principle based on Lyapunov functions introduced in Bhatnagar and Liu (2020 Math. Models Methods Appl. Sci. 30 891-916). A key finding of this work is that the inclusion of linear damping effectively removes the initial density lower bound previously required in the undamped case (Tadmor and Tan 2022 SIAM J. Math. Anal. 54 4277-96) in certain regimes, allowing for global regularity even in the presence of vacuum or arbitrarily low density. Furthermore, for subcritical initial data, we prove an exponential decay rate to the equilibrium state. Our results unify and extend existing theories for 1D Euler-Poisson system and undamped multidimensional EMA system with radial symmetry.
papers.comments: This is the version to appear in Nonlinearity; several major/minor errors have been corrected

papers.title: Transitive Sets of Mutually Orthogonal Latin Squares
papers.abstract: Write $n=\prod_{i=1}^u p_i^{a_i}$ for the prime factorization of $n$. We prove that a net of order $n$ admitting a point-transitive group of automorphisms preserving each parallel class has at most $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}+1)$ parallel classes. This extends Jungnickel's sharp bound for translation nets. Equivalently, the maximum number of jointly cell-transitive mutually orthogonal Latin squares of order $n$ is $\min_i(p_i^{a_i}-1)$. An explicit Latin square of order nine answers affirmatively Krotov and Potapov's question about the existence of an isotopically transitive, non-topolinear Latin square.

papers.title: D-ripALM: A Tuning-friendly Decentralized Relative-Type Inexact Proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method
papers.abstract: This paper proposes D-ripALM, a Decentralized relative-type inexact proximal Augmented Lagrangian Method for consensus convex optimization over multi-agent networks. D-ripALM adopts a double-loop distributed optimization framework that accommodates a wide range of inner solvers, enabling efficient treatment of both smooth and nonsmooth objectives. D-ripALM employs a relative-type error criterion to regulate the switching between inner and outer iterations, replacing a prescribed absolute tolerance sequence with a single relative tolerance parameter. Moreover, we establish rigorous convergence guarantees for D-ripALM under general convexity assumptions, without requiring smoothness or strong convexity conditions commonly imposed in the distributed optimization literature. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets demonstrate that a restarted variant of D-ripALM achieves competitive computational efficiency and solution accuracy relative to representative decentralized algorithms.

papers.title: On the Coupled Cluster Doubles Truncation Variety of Four Electrons
papers.abstract: We extend recent algebro-geometric results for coupled cluster theory of quantum many-body systems to the truncation varieties arising from the doubles approximation (CCD), focusing on the first genuinely nonlinear doubles regime of four electrons. Since this doubles truncation variety does not coincide with previously studied varieties, we initiate a systematic investigation of its basic algebro-geometric invariants. We show that for $4$ electrons in $n \geq 13$ orbitals, the CCD truncation variety is not a complete intersection, and we present numerical and symbolic evidence that for the remaining cases it is a complete intersection defined by $\binom{n-4}{4}$ quadrics. Using representation-theoretic arguments, we uncover a Pfaffian structure governing the quadratic relations that define the truncation variety for any $n$, and show that an exact tensor product factorization holds in the distinguished limit of disconnected doubles. We connect these structural results to the computation of the beryllium insertion into molecular hydrogen ({Be$\cdots$H$_2$ $\to$ H--Be--H}), a small but computationally challenging bond formation process where multiconfigurational effects become pronounced.
papers.comments: 26 pages, 6 figures, code stored in Zenodo. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: A type theory for invertibility in weak $ω$-categories
papers.abstract: We present a conservative extension ICaTT of the dependent type theory Catt for weak $ω$-categories with a type witnessing coinductive invertibility of cells. This extension allows for a concise description of the ``walking equivalence'' as a context, and of a set of maps characterising $ω$-equifibrations as substitutions. We provide an implementation of our theory, which we use to formalise basic properties of invertible cells. These properties allow us to give semantics of ICaTT in marked weak $ω$-categories, building a fibrant marked $ω$-category out of every model of ICaTT.

papers.title: Countability Properties of Weakly Compact Sets in Asymmetric Locally Convex Spaces
papers.abstract: A dual pair formulation for asymmetric locally convex spaces is introduced that strictly generalises the ordinary vector space setting. The concept of a polar topology carries over to the asymmetric case and some familiar results are reproduced or generalised such as the bipolar theorem and a Mackey-Arens type theorem. The implications of weak compactness and countability properties are studied and appear intimately connected to separation properties. An asymmetric analogue $C_a(K)$ of the well-known space $C_p(K)$ is introduced and the properties of (relatively) countably respectively sequentially) compact subspaces are investigated. In particular, it is shown that $C_a([0,1])$ is not angelic. However, for Hausdorff subspaces, the different compactness conditions are equivalent and imply the Fréchet-Urysohn property. Moreover, an analogue of the Eberlein-Šmulian theorem holds in asymmetrically normed spaces.

papers.title: Exponential Lower Bounds for 2-query Relaxed Locally Decodable Codes
papers.abstract: Locally Decodable Codes (LDCs) are error-correcting codes $C\colonΣ^n\rightarrow Σ^m,$ encoding \emph{messages} in $Σ^n$ to \emph{codewords} in $Σ^m$, with super-fast decoding algorithms. They are important mathematical objects in many areas of theoretical computer science, yet the best constructions so far have codeword length $m$ that is super-polynomial in $n$, for codes with constant query complexity and constant alphabet size, while tolerating a constant-fraction of errors. In a very surprising result, Ben-Sasson, Goldreich, Harsha, Sudan, and Vadhan (SICOMP 2006) show how to construct a relaxed version of LDCs (RLDCs) with constant query complexity and slightly super-linear codeword length over the binary alphabet, and used them to obtain significantly-improved constructions of Probabilistically Checkable Proofs. In this work, we prove an exponential lower bound on the length of Hamming RLDCs making $2$ queries (even adaptively) over the binary alphabet. This answers a question explicitly raised by Gur and Lachish (SICOMP 2021) and is the first exponential lower bound for RLDCs. Combined with the results of Ben-Sasson et al., our result exhibits a "phase-transition"-type behavior on the codeword length for some constant-query complexity. We achieve these lower bounds via a transformation of RLDCs to LDCs, using a careful analysis of restrictions of message bits that fix codeword bits.
papers.comments: arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2209.08688

papers.title: Weighted boundedness for the maximal operator associated with matrices
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness on $L^p(w)$ of the maximal operator $M_{A^{-1}}$, defined by $M_{A^{-1}}f(x)=Mf(A^{-1}x)$, that is, the maximal of Hardy-Littlewood composed with a invertible matrix $A$. We present two different results of boundedness and provide a characterization for a particular case of matrices. The main novelty lies in examples illustrating the difference between the class of weights with a matrix, $\mathcal{A}_{A,p}$, and the classical Muckenhoupt weight class, $\mathcal{A}_{p}$. Finally, we extend these results to the fractional framework, considering the fractional maximal operator $M_{α, A^{-1}}$.
papers.comments: 13 pages, minor revision: improved introduction, added Proposition 2.5

papers.title: Cohen-Macaulay squarefree powers of edge ideals of very well-covered graphs
papers.abstract: Let $G$ be a graph with edge ideal $I(G)$. For $q\ge 1$, the $q$th squarefree power $I(G)^{[q]}$ is the Stanley-Reisner ideal of the $q$-matching-free complex $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$, whose faces are the vertex sets containing no $q$ pairwise disjoint edges. We determine exactly which squarefree powers of the edge ideal of a very well-covered graph are Cohen-Macaulay: if $G$ has $2n$ vertices, then $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ is Cohen-Macaulay if and only if $q=n$, or $q=1$ and $G$ is Cohen-Macaulay, or $G=W(H)$ is a whisker graph and $q \le \left\lfloor \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rfloor$. The answer is independent of the field. The proof rests on a rigidity theorem: among very well-covered graphs, only whisker graphs have a sequentially Cohen-Macaulay squarefree power strictly between the first and the last. For whisker graphs we show that $\mathsf{MF}^q(W(H))$ is vertex decomposable for $q \le \left\lceil \frac{\operatorname{girth}(H)}{2} \right\rceil$, and we express the depth and the regularity of every squarefree power through the homology of explicit auxiliary complexes. As a consequence we prove a conjecture of Das, Roy and Saha on the depth of squarefree powers of whisker cycles. Finally, for every graph with a perfect matching, we compute the top homology of $\mathsf{MF}^q(G)$ and determine when the regularity of $R/I(G)^{[q]}$ attains its maximal possible value.
papers.comments: Substantially revised and expanded version, with a new title. We establish a complete classification of Cohen-Macaulay squarefree powers of edge ideals of very well-covered graphs, prove new rigidity and vertex-decomposability results, resolve a conjecture of Das, Roy and Saha, and obtain new results on depth, regularity, and top homology

papers.title: Oort's conjecture on automorphisms of generic supersingular abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We prove Oort's conjecture that generically on the supersingular locus of the moduli space of principally polarized abelian varieties of genus g and in characteristic p, the automorphism group of the universal principally polarized abelian variety consists only of $\pm 1$, unless g=2, 3 or 4 and p=2. On the way, we provide an explicit description of the a=1-locus in the Rapoport-Zink space of principally polarized supersingular p-divisible groups of any dimension g. We also prove analogous results for generic automorphism groups on moduli spaces of supersingular p-divisible groups with and without polarization.
papers.comments: 20 pages; v2: exposition improved, minor corrections; v3: update due to an update of the paper by Karemaker-Yu [2406.19748], where it turned out that the conjecture is actually false for the case g=4, p=2, minor other corrections

papers.title: A Block Hierarchy for Rate-Distortion and Dispersion of Binary Markov Sources
papers.abstract: The finite-length rate penalty for compressing a binary Markov source under Hamming distortion remains open in general. To study this penalty, we use memoryless sources that draw independent $K$-symbol blocks from the Markov law. We determine the rate and tilted-information variance per symbol at every distortion for positively correlated two-symbol blocks of arbitrary stationary bias and for symmetric three- and four-symbol blocks. For a symmetric chain with flip probability $0<p<1/2$, we prove that the normalized variance converges to a positive limit at every interior distortion where the Markov rate-distortion function is differentiable. At positive distortions up to Gray's critical distortion, this limit equals the source varentropy rate and yields a second-order coding converse for a single Markov path. We conjecture that the limit is the operational dispersion of the Markov source. Matching achievability remains open.
papers.comments: 30 pages, 13 figures. Retitled and substantially revised. Replaces the single-letter analysis with a block hierarchy. Proves convergence of the normalized block variance for symmetric persistent sources and a low-distortion second-order converse. Code, data, and proof companion: https://github.com/ANRGUSC/markov-block-hierarchy

papers.title: Convergence Rate of a Functional Learning Method for Conditional Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We consider a stochastic optimization problem involving two random variables: a context variable $X$ and a dependent variable $Y$. The objective is to minimize the expected value of a nonlinear loss functional applied to the conditional expectation $\mathbb{E}[f(X, Y,β) \mid X]$, where $f$ is a nonlinear function and $β$ represents the decision variables. We focus on the practically important setting in which direct sampling from the conditional distribution of $Y \mid X$ is infeasible, and only a stream of i.i.d. observation pairs $\{(X^k, Y^k)\}_{k=0,1,2,\ldots}$ is available. In our approach, the conditional expectation is approximated within a prespecified parametric function class. We analyze a simultaneous learning-and-optimization algorithm that jointly estimates the conditional expectation and optimizes the outer objective. Using a specially designed measure of non-optimality, combining the squared norm of the objective function's gradient and the mean square error of the auxiliary parametric model, we establish that the method achieves a convergence rate of order $\mathcal{O}\big(1/\sqrt{N}\big)$, where $N$ denotes the number of observed pairs. The rate holds in expectation when the auxiliary model is linear in its parameters, which includes linear architectures with bounded features, and in probability for general smooth models.

papers.title: Stabilization of highly nonlinear hybrid stochastic differential delay equations by periodically intermittent feedback controls based on discrete time observations with asynchronous switching
papers.abstract: This paper extends the stabilization analysis of highly nonlinear time delay systems to the case where periodic intermittent control, discrete time observation, and sampling-induced asynchronous mode switching coexist, and establishes corresponding moment estimates and exponential stability criteria. To overcome the difficulties emerged due to intermittent control and discrete time observations with asynchronous switching, we introduce a discontinuous Lyapunov function and account for the effect of the discontinuities of the intermittent control function at switching instants, thereby establishing the moment exponential stability of the controlled system. Finally, an example is presented to interpret the conclusion.

papers.title: The Value of Information in Resource-Constrained Pricing
papers.abstract: Dynamic pricing with resource constraints requires balancing exploration of unknown demand patterns against exploitation of known information to maximize revenue. We develop algorithms for this problem across different information regimes. Products share perishable resources, and the firm posts prices and observes the realized requests, which may exceed the remaining capacity. In the full-information setting, a residual-correction policy that solves the fluid problem once attains $O(\log T)$ regret with bounded prices and arbitrary-rank resource matrices. In the no-information setting, deterministic exploration followed by a certainty-equivalent policy attains $O(\sqrt T)$ regret when the limiting fluid solution is nondegenerate. In the informed-price setting, given an initial price-demand estimate, a feedback controller learns the implementing prices without estimating the slope matrix if the slope matrix is symmetric, a set containing it is known in advance, the informed price is aligned with the resource constraints, and an inverse-image condition holds. A selector chooses between the informed-price algorithm and the no-information algorithm from historical data. Its regret bound includes observation error, misalignment, inventory exits, and periods on the fixed price. We further show how offline surrogate models reduce the regret of the learning policy through variance reduction, even when misspecified. The bound includes calibration and screen failures, and the regret is reduced for all sufficiently large horizons. We finally demonstrate the empirical performances of our policies through complete numerical experiments.

papers.title: Low regularity potentials in heterogeneous Cahn--Hilliard functionals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study the prototypical model of liquid-liquid phase separation, the Cahn-Hilliard functional, in a highly irregular setting. Specifically, we analyze potentials with low regularity vanishing on space-dependent wells. Under remarkably weak hypotheses, we establish a robust compactness result. Strengthening the regularity of the wells and of the growth of the potential close to the wells only slightly, we completely characterize the asymptotic behavior of the associated family of functionals through a $Γ$-convergence analysis. As a notable technical result, we prove the existence of geodesics for a degenerate metric and establish a uniform bound on their Euclidean length.

papers.title: Elephant Random Walks on Coverings of Dipole Graphs
papers.abstract: In the present paper, we introduce and analyze elephant random walks (ERWs) on bipartite periodic lattices arising as coverings of dipole graphs. We focus on lattices whose admissible step directions in the two parts of the bipartition are negatives of each other and disjoint. On such graphs, we define an ERW in which each step is chosen by referring to the entire history of the walk. The ERW on the hexagonal lattice is a prototypical example of our model. The definition and asymptotic analysis of such ERWs are not straightforward because both depend strongly on the underlying geometric structure. Our analysis is based on a combination of the Pólya-type urn techniques and the martingale approach, two standard methods for analyzing ERWs. We find that the counting process of the ERW forms a Pólya-type urn with two-periodic generating matrices. By analyzing such urn models, we show the strong law of large numbers for the counting process. Combining the result for the counting process with the martingale approach, we derive the strong laws of large numbers with non-standard normalizations and central limit theorems for the position process of the ERW in the diffusive and critical regimes, as well as almost sure and $L^2$ scaling limits in the superdiffusive regime.
papers.comments: The assumptions concerning independence have been revised, and minor errors have also been corrected

papers.title: The Bollobás--Nikiforov inequality for complete multipartite graphs, with remarks on the $K_4$-free case
papers.abstract: Bollobás and Nikiforov conjectured that every graph $G \neq K_n$ with $m$ edges and clique number $ω$ satisfies $λ_1^2(G) + λ_2^2(G) \leq 2(1 - 1/ω)m$, where $λ_1(G) \geq λ_2(G)$ are the two largest adjacency eigenvalues. We give a short self-contained proof of the inequality for complete multipartite graphs, based on a quadratic-form identity which shows that $λ_2 \leq 0$, and we determine the equality cases in this class. We show that equality in the conjecture is attained by a wider family than the Turán graphs, namely by disjoint unions of two complete bipartite graphs, or of two balanced complete $r$-partite graphs of possibly different orders. For $K_4$-free graphs we record the cases that follow from known results, with corrected attributions, and we give examples showing that three natural lines of attack fail: a Hoffman-type eigenvalue bound for graphs with large independence number, a spectral stability statement for connected graphs, and Zykov symmetrization in an arbitrary direction.
papers.comments: v4: substantially revised. Corrects errors in v1-v3 (equality cases, Hoffman-type bound, stability conjecture, Zykov lemma, attributions); the claimed result for dense K4-free graphs is withdrawn. 10 pages

papers.title: A Partially Parabolic Damage-Driven Inflammation Model: Threshold Dynamics and Linear Spreading
papers.abstract: We study a partially parabolic reaction--diffusion--chemotaxis model of damage--inflammation feedback motivated by Duchenne muscular dystrophy. The model couples functional and damaged tissue with effective macrophage activity and a damage-induced inflammatory signal. The invariant tissue simplex bounds the damage source and, together with parabolic estimates, yields global well-posedness and dissipativity in every spatial dimension covered by the regularity assumptions, for arbitrary chemotactic sensitivity. A dimensionless feedback threshold separates resolution to a damage-free dystrophin-deficient state from the existence of a positive damage equilibrium in the spatially homogeneous system. On bounded connected domains, we prove resolution at and below the threshold and, above it, uniform componentwise persistence with spatially uniform lower bounds for initial data with at least one nonzero active component. We derive a candidate linear spreading speed for localized damage and establish a nonlinear upper spreading bound in the absence of chemotaxis. Numerical front speeds agree closely with the linear prediction in the simulations.

papers.title: Geometric bounds for Steklov and weighted Neumann eigenvalues on Euclidean domains
papers.abstract: We obtain sharp upper bounds for the first two nonzero Steklov eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean spaces of dimension $d \geq 7$ under a natural normalization involving volume and boundary measure. These bounds are derived from a characterization of optimal domains and weights for the first two nonzero weighted Neumann eigenvalues. In dimensions $3 \leq d \leq 6$, we obtain upper bounds that are not sharp. We further establish strict upper bounds with sharp constants for all higher Steklov eigenvalues on simply connected planar domains with continuous boundary and finite boundary length. Beyond the second nonzero eigenvalue, these bounds were previously known only for smooth planar domains.
papers.comments: 16 pages; minor typo corrections; to appear in Int. Math. Res. Not

papers.title: An Adaptive Log-Laguerre Spectral Method for the Radial Dirac Equation: Resolving Asymptotic Decay and Core Singularities in Atomic Calculations
papers.abstract: The high-precision solution of the radial Dirac equation is fundamental to relativistic quantum chemistry, essential for reliable pseudopotential generation and all-electron electronic structure methods. Capturing both the non-polynomial singularities at the origin and the state-dependent asymptotic decay on semi-infinite domains presents a significant computational challenge. In this work, we propose the Adaptive Log-Laguerre Spectral Method (ALLSM), a novel coupled spectral-element solver that seamlessly integrates three advanced mathematical methodologies into a unified framework. Specifically, Generalized Log-Orthogonal Functions (GLOFs) are deployed in the near-core region to intrinsically approximate complex $r^s$ singular behaviors without requiring prior knowledge of the exact analytical exponent $s$. Concurrently, an adaptive Laguerre spectral method is employed to dynamically capture diverse exponential tails on $[0, \infty)$, avoiding artificial domain truncation. To structurally guarantee spectral purity across this bipartite basis, the framework rigorously incorporates the Inverse Dirac Operator Method (IDOM), effectively eliminating variational collapse and spurious states. Validated across diverse physical regimes, including Coulomb, finite-nucleus, and screened potentials, the proposed solver restores exponential convergence and consistently achieves relative accuracies of $10^{-10}$. This work provides a robust, pollution-free computational kernel for atomic structure calculations, establishing a highly reliable numerical standard for complex molecular simulations.

papers.title: Infinite graphs with finite metric dimension
papers.abstract: We study the metric dimension (strong and weak) of connected infinite graphs. In particular, our main interest is characterizing infinite graphs with finite dimension. Our main results: (1) graphs with more than one end have infinite strong dimension; (2) for locally finite graphs with a finite number of cycles, the weak dimension is finite if and only if the graph has finitely many vertices of degree at least three, and the strong dimension is finite if and only if the graph has one end and finitely many vertices of degree at least three.

papers.title: Noncommutative Geometry, Spectral Asymptotics, and Semiclassical Analysis, I. Main Results
papers.abstract: In this paper, we combine techniques from functional analysis and spectral theory to obtain semiclassical Weyl laws and extensions of Connes' integration formula for a large class of spectral triples. These results generalize and simplify recent work of McDonald--Sukochev--Zanin: all regularity assumptions and dimension restrictions are removed, and their Tauberian condition is replaced by a weaker spectral condition, Condition~(W), which holds in far greater generality. We also establish Tauberian criteria for Condition~(W) involving zeta functions and heat traces, as sought by Alain Connes. The results are illustrated on bounded Euclidean domains, closed Riemannian manifolds, the Steklov problem, and quantum tori. In the latter setting they resolve a conjecture of Edward McDonald and the author. This is the first part of a two-part work. The proofs of the main technical results are given in Part II.
papers.comments: v4: the previous version has been split into 2 papers. Part 1 contains the main results. Part 2 contains the main operator-theoretic tools

papers.title: Rational relative sectional category
papers.abstract: We develop an algebraic model for the relative sectional category of a continuous map in rational homotopy theory using commutative differential graded algebras (CDGAs). Our main result establishes that for formal maps, the rational relative sectional category can be computed purely from cohomology, using ideal nilpotency. We also show that this equality may fail in general topological settings. Applying this framework, we obtain purely algebraic characterizations for the rational Lusternik-Schnirelmann category and the rational higher topological complexity of a map. Finally, we provide an algebraic description of the rational homotopic distance between formal maps.
papers.comments: Examples are corrected. some other changes are done
papers.journal_ref: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 2026

papers.title: Root laminations of arbitrary degree
papers.abstract: This paper studies the space of degree $d>1$ invariant q-laminations, i.e., geodesic laminations invariant under the $d$-tupling map of the circle and associated with equivalence relations. Our main construction associates a q-lamination with any degree $d$ critical portrait \emph{in a canonical way}. Even though somewhat technical, this is the initial step in the program of classification of all degree $d$ invariant q-laminations.
papers.comments: 71 pages, no figures; it is a second version of the article in which an inaccuracy was corrected and some proofs were expanded. We wish to thank Prof. Yan Gao for drawing our attention to this issue

papers.title: The maximum Cox complexity of a Fano-type variety and the Mukai conjecture
papers.abstract: We define an intrinsic invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(\cdot)$, the maximum Cox complexity, of Fano-type varieties $X$. We prove $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\in\mathbb{Q}_{\geq 0}$ and $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)=0$ if and only if $X$ is toric. We then apply this invariant to the Mukai conjecture, which characterises powers of projective spaces among smooth Fano varieties in terms of $\dim(X)$, the Picard number $ρ(X)$, and the Fano index $i(X)$. All klt Fano varieties $X$ canonically embed into a projective toric variety $Z$ via their Cox ring. When $Z$ is smooth, we call $X$ ambiently smooth. We prove the Mukai conjecture for ambiently smooth Fano varieties by establishing the stronger inequality: $\dim(X)+ρ(X)-i(X)ρ(X)\geqγ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)\geq 0$. Notably, 45% of the deformation families of smooth Fano threefolds have an ambiently smooth member. For a Fano-type variety $X$, the invariant $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$ is defined using coefficient sums of anticanonical divisors supported on the divisors corresponding to minimal homogeneous generators of the Cox ring. Our proof proceeds by reducing the Cox ring to positive characteristic, using strong F-regularity to obtain the coefficients of an anticanonical divisor, and the F-pure threshold to establish the nonnegativity of $γ_{\mathrm{Cox}}(X)$.
papers.comments: We explicitly introduce and highlight the maximum Cox complexity, an invariant which already played a central role in the previous version. The core results are the same as in the previous version

papers.title: Benders Cut Filtering for Affine Potential-Based Flow Problems with Robustness Scenarios and Topology Switching
papers.abstract: Many large-scale optimization problems decompose into a master problem and scenario subproblems. Benders decomposition exploits this structure by iteratively solving the subproblems and adding constraints, called Benders cuts, to the master problem. We study Benders cut filtering: given a set of Benders cuts produced in one iteration, which subset should be added to the master problem? Adding all generated cuts can cause rapid master problem growth, whereas retaining fewer cuts may require more Benders iterations. To our knowledge, few prior works have studied this question for Benders cuts. Classical cut filtering techniques require modification because Benders cuts enforce constraints omitted from the master problem, whereas conventional cutting planes are optional inequalities that strengthen the relaxation. We propose violation-based filtering, diversity-based filtering via k-medoids clustering on cosine distances, and a hybrid that selects a most-violated cut per cluster. We compare these strategies with no filtering, random filtering, and our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector on an affine potential-based flow problem with topology switching and robustness scenarios. On instances solved by all configurations, our hybrid approach reduces the shifted geometric mean solve time by about 45% compared to no filtering, and by 39% compared to our adaptation of SCIP's hybrid cut selector. While violation-based filtering achieves a similar runtime, the hybrid approach requires about 17% fewer callback rounds. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of Benders cut filtering on this problem class and motivate evaluation in other domains.

papers.title: Supercriticality of the SIRS on random networks
papers.abstract: We analyze the supercritical regime of the SIRS process (Susceptible-Infected-Recovered-Susceptible) on random graphs and Galton-Watson trees. Our results provide a three-part characterization of this process: first, we prove that even on finite sparse graphs, the epidemic can survive for an exponentially long time. On heavy-tailed networks with power-law-like exponents, we show that this holds for the entire range of parameters. Notably, while contemporary works establish a stretched exponential survival time for power-law networks, our approach provides the optimal bound of order $e^{Θ(n)}$ via a different approach. Finally, for infinite trees, we establish sufficient conditions for strong survival, proving that the root is re-infected infinitely often even for light-tailed degree distributions like the Poisson distribution.
papers.comments: 28 pages, Section 3 added, major changes in the statement and proof of Theorem 1.3

papers.title: SENECA: Small-Sample Discrete Entropy Estimation via Self-Consistent Missing Mass
papers.abstract: Discrete entropy estimation is a classic information theory problem, wherein the average information content of a discrete random variable is estimated from samples alone. Naive approaches, such as the plugin method, fail to account for the probability mass associated with members of the random variable's support that are unobserved in a given sample, known as the "missing mass." The resulting systemic underestimation is particularly problematic when data is time-consuming or costly to gather. We propose SENECA, an entropy estimation scheme based on a novel "self-consistent" missing mass calculation. Extensive numerical experiments indicate that our approach outperforms many state-of-the-art alternatives overall in the small-sample setting. We then apply SENECA to two practical use cases, namely biodiversity estimation and the detection of incorrect large language model responses, where our method is competitive with domain-specific approaches. Our work advances SENECA as an effective drop-in replacement for small-sample entropy estimation, with broad utility across several domains.

papers.title: Modeling sequential cognitive states via population level cortical dynamics
papers.abstract: In this work, we propose a mathematical framework for cyclic and sequential patterns of brain activity, combining heteroclinic dynamics with discrete neural-field models. Under explicit structural and positivity assumptions on the prescribed activity patterns, we show that the resulting spatially discrete neural-field system supports neither heteroclinic cycles nor nonconstant periodic orbits. Heteroclinic dynamics, on the other hand, arise in Lotka--Volterra-type systems, but these equations do not directly correspond to neuronal processes. To bridge these descriptions, we use a $C^1$ version of the Universal Approximation Theorem to approximate a target vector field by a neural network interpretable as a high-dimensional Amari-type neural-field system. Each periodic solution of the reduced dynamics admits a unique periodic realization at the population level with the same minimal period. For three-dimensional heteroclinic targets, we establish sufficient conditions ensuring that the approximating vector field admits a unique hyperbolic attracting periodic orbit in a trapping channel surrounding the original heteroclinic cycle. As a proof of concept, we apply this construction to a Lotka--Volterra-type target phenomenologically representing sequential network activations associated with focused-attention meditation.

papers.title: Information Theory and Statistical Learning
papers.abstract: This manuscript contains preprint of a chapter in the forthcoming third edition of Cover and Thomas's Elements of Information Theory, posted with permission from Wiley. For feedback, please contact abbas@ee.stanford.edu. Learning and information theory intersect in both model training and the characterization of fundamental performance limits. This manuscript provides a concise and accessible treatment of the first intersection, requiring only basic background in information theory and statistics at the senior undergraduate / first-year graduate level. End-of-chapter exercises make the material well suited for classroom use as well as self-study. The chapter focuses on the role of divergence measures in model training, with examples ranging from linear and logistic regression to autoregressive models, variational autoencoders, diffusion models, and score-based models. In particular, the treatment of the generative diffusion model provides a more systematic and explicit derivation than is typical in the literature.

papers.title: Thresholds for Tic-Tac-Toe on Finite Affine Spaces
papers.abstract: We study the strong positional game in which two players alternately claim points of $\F_q^m$ and the first to complete an affine $n$-subspace wins. We distinguish the first winning dimension $τ(n,q)$ from the eventual winning threshold $T(n,q)$, without assuming monotonicity in $m$. Affine Ramsey theory proves finiteness, while the Erdős-Selfridge criterion and explicit geometric strategies give lower bounds. In the binary case, a quantitative form of the classical quotient argument yields $T(n,2)\le2^{n-1}+n$, with a corresponding bound for any number of colors. A plane-counting recursion gives further multicolor and extremal estimates. We prove $τ(2,2)=T(2,2)=4$ and show that every $31$-point subset of $\F_2^6$ contains an affine $3$-subspace. This gives an elementary proof of the known equality $\AR_2(3;2)=6$ and implies $τ(3,2)=T(3,2)\in\{5,6\}$. Previously known planar outcomes are recovered within the same framework.

papers.title: Shape theory for condensed anima
papers.abstract: We give different perspectives on the notion of shape for condensed anima. We prove that it recovers more classical notions of shape not only for all locally compact Hausdorff but also locally contractible spaces. These recovering statements imply and extend comparison results on sheaf and condensed cohomology by Clausen-Scholze and Haine. Another homotopy-theoretical direction for condensed anima are their condensed homotopy groups. Connected to this, we give a description of the underlying topological group functor on condensed groups via quasi-topological groups.
papers.comments: Updated version, an incorrect statement was removed and corresponding results adjusted, typos corrected, order of chapters changed

papers.title: Algorithms for Computing Set Tolerances: Theory, Computational Analysis and Applications
papers.abstract: The regular set tolerance is an important term in sensitivity analysis. For combinatorial sum problems, e.g., the Traveling Salesman Problem, Shortest Path Problem and Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, it determines how much the sum of the costs of the elements of a set can be increased while ensuring that all current optimal solutions remain optimal. The regular set lower tolerance determines how much the sum of the costs of the elements of a set can be decreased while ensuring that the objective value of the optimal solution is not changed. We investigate general methods for computing regular (upper and lower) set tolerances in combinatorial sum problems. For the upper tolerance, we present a linear programming approach, and for the lower tolerances, three linear programming approaches, where the last two are novel and lead to recursive procedures for computation of the lower tolerances of all subsets of the given ground set. We give new upper bounds for set lower tolerances. For both upper and lower tolerances, we give an exact formula for sets of cardinality 2 and 3. Furthermore, we computationally compare and analyze our introduced tolerance LPs. Finally, we consider the computation of tolerances for the Minimum Spanning Tree Problem, give a formula for single tolerances, a lower bound for regular set upper tolerances and an exact formula for regular set lower tolerances.

papers.title: Moduli of semistable Lie algebroid connections and twisted Higgs bundles
papers.abstract: We study integrable Lie algebroid connections and twisted Higgs fields on vector bundles and principal bundles over smooth projective families of complex curves. Under suitable hypotheses, we construct quasi-projective moduli spaces of semistable principal bundles equipped with these structures and prove that their formation commutes with arbitrary base change. We also characterize algebraically integrable transitive Lie algebroids on smooth irreducible complex varieties as Atiyah algebroids of principal bundles whose gauge groupoids are representable by separated schemes of finite type. Further results concern the local freeness of twisted Higgs sheaves and neutral Tannakian descriptions of the associated categories.
papers.comments: Substantially updated to fix many mistakes and gaps in the previous version, title modified. Comments are welcome

papers.title: Higher Rank-Support Weights and $(q,m)$-Polymatroids
papers.abstract: The aim of this paper is to develop a $(q,m)$-polymatroidal approach to higher supports and higher rank-weight enumerators of Delsarte rank-metric codes. In this framework, we establish rank-metric analogs of several fundamental results known for matroids and linear codes. We describe minimal higher supports in terms of cocircuits of suitable truncations of the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid, and obtain a polymatroidal interpretation of generalized minimum rank weights and their Singleton-type bound. We also prove that the associated $(q,m)$-polymatroid and the higher support distributions determine each other. On the enumerative side, we establish a Greene-type identity relating higher rank-weight enumerators to the rank generating function, and conversely show that the full sequence of higher rank-weight enumerators determines this function. As the main application, we prove MacWilliams-type identities for higher rank-weight enumerators by first deriving a duality formula for higher weight polynomials of $(q,m)$-polymatroids and then applying it to a rank-metric code and its dual.

papers.title: Self-similarity and diffusive limits for linear kinetic equations: a Wild sum approach
papers.abstract: We prove that linear collisional kinetic equations in the whole space without confinement mechanism display a long-time self-similar behaviour. This drastically improves the recently known results (decay estimates) about the solutions in such a context, providing the first result regarding this self-similar behaviour. As a consequence, we also establish a uniform-in-time convergence of the suitably rescaled solutions to their diffusion limit, which is also new. The class of equations considered includes some BGK type equations, some kinetic nonlocal Fokker--Planck-type equations and some kinetic (possibly fractional) Fokker--Planck equations, for which we are able to write explicitly solutions through a Wild sum (or Dyson series) or we can manage some accurate computations on the Fourier side.
papers.comments: 55 pages. v2: fixed some issues and improved the clarity of the manuscript

papers.title: Lower bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of expressible sets
papers.abstract: We obtain positive lower bounds on the Hausdorff dimension of sets of real numbers given by expressions of the form $\sum_{n=1}^\infty \frac{1}{a_n b_n}$, where $b_n$ satisfies some growth condition and $a_n$ lies in some set, possibly depending on $n$. As a consequence of our results, some of the irrational numbers arising from Erdős' celebrated construction from 1976 are not Liouville numbers.

papers.title: Geometric Properties of positive solutions of Lane-Emden problems on convex domains of $§^2$
papers.abstract: We study positive solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu = u^p$ in a uniformly convex domain $Ω\subset §^2$, $u= 0$ on $\partialΩ.$ For $p=1$, we assume that the right-hand side is replaced by $λ_1 u$, where $λ_1$ is the first eigenvalue of $-Δ$ on $Ω$ with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. We prove that for $0 \leq p < 1$ the unique positive solution $u$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly concave in $Ω$, while for $1 < p \leq 3$ every positive solution $u$ which belongs to the connected component of the least-energy branch of solutions issued from $p=1$ is such that $u^{\frac{1-p}{2}}$ is strictly convex in $Ω$.

papers.title: Multidimensional Reconciliation in Continuous-Variable QKD: Review, Coding Schemes, and Open-Source Simulation
papers.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) requires highly efficient reconciliation techniques to operate at low signal-to-noise ratios and long distances. Multidimensional reconciliation addresses this challenge by transforming the physical Gaussian quantum channel into a virtual binary-input additive white Gaussian noise (BIAWGN) channel, enabling the use of modern errorcorrecting codes. In this work, we review the principles of multidimensional reconciliation, with a particular focus on high-dimensional constructions beyond the algebraic dimensions 1, 2, 4, 8. We describe the construction of the virtual channel, discuss practical coding schemes for reverse reconciliation, and analyse their integration with linear error-correcting codes. We also present an opensource simulation framework, HDirac, implementing multidimensional reconciliation for arbitrary dimensions, and use it to evaluate state-of-the-art LDPC codes. The results highlight key trade-offs between dimension, reconciliation efficiency, and frame error rate, providing practical guidance for CV-QKD system design.
papers.comments: 15 pages, 8 figures. Link to the open-source project: https://github.com/aff3ct/HDirac

papers.title: Optimal constants of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators
papers.abstract: We study optimal constants and extremizers of smoothing estimates for quantum harmonic oscillators. In particular, we establish harmonic oscillator analogues of free particle results due to Simon (1992), Bez and Sugimoto (2015), and Bez et al. (2015).
papers.comments: 16 pages. Revised according to the referee's report

papers.title: Cheeger-type inequalities for the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian
papers.abstract: We study the second largest spectral gap from $1$ of the normalized Laplacian of a graph, a quantity that appears in the literature in connection with random walks, expander graphs, and Ramanujan graphs. We relate it to the classical Cheeger and dual Cheeger constants, and we introduce a new Cheeger-type constant admitting a probabilistic interpretation in terms of two-step random walks. For this constant, we establish sharp inequalities analogous to the classical Cheeger inequalities.
papers.comments: We added a note in v2 regarding the novelty of our results

papers.title: Low-Rank Acceleration of the Operator Fourier Transform
papers.abstract: We develop a numerical algorithm for the efficient solution or approximation of solutions to the Helmholtz equation on a structured grid in two dimensions. We make use of the Operator Fourier Transform (OFT) and a low-rank cross approximation scheme (Cross-DEIM) to decompose the problem into an integral over a pseudo-time of solutions to the Schrödinger equation. The OFT is a framework for solving operator equations like fractional Laplacian equations or the Helmholtz equation, when the latter is written as a product of two paraxial operators. The main computational cost in the OFT is the solution to the Schrödinger equation, especially when the dimension or mesh resolution is high. In this work, we alleviate this cost by utilizing a low-rank method. Such methods aim to beat the curse of dimensionality when low-rank structures are present in the solution. For a problem with a constant coefficient we show that the resulting solver converges at second order in the pseudo-time step and reaches the accuracy of the direct solution of the discretized linear system, which is limited by the second-order finite-difference discretization in space, while keeping the solution in low-rank form. The ranks of the accumulated solution change little as the grid is refined, which suggests a cost per time step that grows nearly linearly with the number of grid points in each direction.

papers.title: A Resurgent Analytic Framework for Indicial Umbral Calculus via Mellin-Barnes and Borel-Laplace Theories
papers.abstract: We introduce the Analytic Umbral Framework (AUF), which gives formal indicial umbral evaluation an analytic meaning through Mellin-Barnes pairings. An auxiliary Borel representative defines a continuous linear action on compatible weighted spaces of analytic ground states. The resulting function is initially defined in a sector of the logarithmic covering. Finite contour displacement recovers the formal umbral coefficients, with remainder estimates distinguishing ordinary asymptotics, strong Gevrey asymptotics and equality with a convergent series. The associated auxiliary Laplace series are resurgent for rational profiles and entire profiles of exponential type. Under explicit spectral conditions, the pairing coincides with the Borel-Laplace sum of the evaluated formal series. An exact spectral transmutation relates exponential and rational representatives and extends to admissible Pólya superpositions. It preserves the analytic value under a compensating change of ground state. A Hankel construction supplies complementary realizations for inverse-Gamma states.
