papers.abstract: Let $L/K$ be an arbitrary Galois extension with group $G$, equipped with the Krull topology. Let $C(G,K)$ denote the $K$-vector space of continuous functions $G\to K$, with $K$ discrete and $G$ acting by left translation. We prove that there exists a $G$-equivariant $K$-linear isomorphism $\varphi:C(G,K)\to L$ such that, for every open subgroup $H$ of $G$, the map $\varphi^H:C(H,L^H)\to L$ induced by extension by zero and extension of scalars is an $H$-equivariant $L^H$-linear isomorphism. This gives a completely normal analogue of Lenstra's infinite normal basis theorem.

papers.title: On the two critical exponents for a dispersive equation with weak dissipation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we study a nonlinear Cauchy problem written in normal form \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u_{tt} + A u+ Bu_t =D|u|^α, & t\geq 0, x \in \mathbb{R}^n\\ u(0,x)=u_0(x),\,u_t(0,x)=u_1(x). \end{cases} \end{equation*} Here~ $Af=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(a(ξ)^2\mathscr{F}f)$, with $a(ξ)$ homogeneous of order $k > 0$ under the assumption that the Hessian matrix of $a(ξ)$ is nonsingular, the operator $Bf=\mathscr{F}^{-1}(b(ξ)\mathscr{F}f)$ represents a weak dissipation, in the sense that $b(ξ) \sim 1$ as $|ξ| \to \infty$ and %, in several models, $D=B$ but we also consider the case $Df=ν\ast (-Δ)^δ(I-Δ)^{-δ}$, with $ν$ a bounded measure and $δ\geq k/2$. We derive $L^p-L^q$ estimates of the linear solution operator to the considered model and we prove the transition from a Fujita-type exponent to a Strauss-type exponent for the global-in-time existence of small data solution for the corresponding nonlinear problems.
papers.comments: This is the final version of the paper, accepted for publication in Annali dell'Università di Ferrara

papers.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

papers.title: The second closed geodesic on Finsler manifolds with $\mathbb{Z}_2$ fundamental group
papers.abstract: Let $(M, F)$ be a compact bumpy Finsler manifold with $π_1(M)=\mathbb{Z}_2$, we prove that there exist at least two distinct non-contractible closed geodesics on $(M, F)$.
papers.comments: Minor revisions of the previous version

papers.title: Dual Quaternion Discrete Linear Canonical Transforms: Theory, Fast Algorithms, and Chirp-Adaptive Filtering for Rigid-Body Pose Signals
papers.abstract: We develop one- and two-dimensional dual quaternion discrete linear canonical transforms (DQ-DLCTs) for rigid-body pose signals, with left-, right-, and two-sided formulations that account for noncommutative kernel ordering. We establish inverse relations, kernel unitarity, energy preservation, perturbation stability, and spatial and frequency convolution relations. A chirp--Fourier--chirp factorization enables fast forward and inverse algorithms using complex FFTs, with two-dimensional complexity $\mathcal O(N_1N_2(\log N_1+\log N_2))$. For pose denoising, we introduce a two-stage chirp-adaptive method that estimates rotation before refining translation while enforcing unit-dual-quaternion constraints. Numerical experiments demonstrate agreement with direct transforms, substantial computational gains, and lower pose errors than the tested baselines on measured sequences and constructed two-dimensional fields. A downstream $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ synchronization study further demonstrates the potential of the proposed preprocessing approach, with performance depending on graph configurations. These results support efficient and geometry-aware processing of rigid-body pose signals.

papers.title: Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
papers.abstract: Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.

papers.title: A Polynomial Criterion for Adaptive Stabilization of Discrete-Time Stochastic Nonlinear Systems with an Unknown Input Gain
papers.abstract: We consider scalar discrete-time systems whose nonlinear function is a linear combination of known power functions with unknown coefficients. The input gain is nonzero and unknown, and the noise is iid zero-mean Gaussian with unknown positive variance. We show that global stabilizability is equivalent to the joint positivity of a family of polynomials determined solely by the power exponents. When this condition holds, a feedback law depending only on the exponents makes the average squared output converge almost surely to the noise variance, the smallest possible value. When the condition fails, every Borel feedback law yields divergence of the output magnitude with positive probability for some fixed parameters and a deterministic initial state.

papers.title: Interior $C^2$ Estimates and a Liouville Theorem for the Complex Monge-Ampère Equation under a Quadratic Lower Bound
papers.abstract: Let $n\ge2$ and let $u$ be a locally bounded plurisubharmonic Bedford-Taylor solution of the complex Monge-Ampère equation $\det(u_{i\bar j})=f$. Assume that in a sufficiently large ball centered at the origin in $\mathbb{C}^{n}$ \[ u(z)\ge δ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|x_i|^2,\qquad x_i=\operatorname{Re}z_{i},\qquad δ>0, \] and $u(0)\leq H$. If $f$ is Dini-continuous, bounded above and bounded away from zero, and satisfies $Δ_{\mathbb {R}}(f^{1/n})\ge-K$ in distributions, we derive an interior bound for the real $C^{2}$ norm on the unit ball $B_{1}(0)$. When $f\equiv1$, every entire solution satisfying $u(z)\geδ\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\operatorname{Re}z_i|^2$ for all $z\in\mathbb{C}^{n}$ and some $δ>0$ is a real quadratic polynomial.

papers.title: Percolation on Bidirected Graphs
papers.abstract: We study bidirected percolation on an undirected graph $G$: each edge is replaced by two oppositely directed edges, each of which is open independently with probability $p$. Two vertices are strongly connected if they are mutually reachable by open directed paths. Let $p_\mathrm{sc}$ denote the threshold for the existence of an infinite strongly connected cluster, and let $p_c$ denote the usual Bernoulli percolation threshold on $G$. On every transitive amenable graph, we prove that $p_\mathrm{sc}=p_c$. In contrast, sufficiently spread-out modifications of every transitive non-amenable graph satisfy $p_\mathrm{sc}>p_c$. We also show that, on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ for all sufficiently large $d$, the expected size of the strongly connected cluster is finite at $p=p_\mathrm{sc}$.

papers.title: The Laplace transform of the stationary measure of the open KPZ equation in the shock region
papers.abstract: The stationary increment measure of the open Kardar-Parisi-Zhang equation on a bounded interval can be represented as the independent sum of a Brownian motion and another process defined via an explicit Radon-Nikodym derivative with respect to the measure induced by a Brownian motion. In the fan region, its finite-dimensional Laplace transform was previously expressed in terms of the continuous dual Hahn process. The main contribution here consists of computing the finite-dimensional Laplace transform for a range of parameters in the shock region by an analytic continuation argument. As an application, we provide a direct proof of the convergence of the finite-dimensional distributions of the increment height function of open WASEP under the stationary measure in the shock region, by computing the convergence of finite-dimensional Laplace transform without relating to the open KPZ equation.
papers.comments: 58 pages; introduction revised, a few references added

papers.title: Identifying codes of Archimedean grids
papers.abstract: An identifying code of a graph is a dominating set $C$ such that the sets $N[v]\cap C$ are pairwise distinct. The minimum density of an identifying code has been studied extensively for several infinite grids. It is known to be $1/4$ for the triangular grid and $7/20$ for the square grid, whereas for the hexagonal grid the problem is still open, between $5/12$ and $53/126$. These three grids are the regular members of the family of the eleven Archimedean grids. In this paper, we start a systematic study of identifying codes in this family. We determine the minimum density for five of the nine Archimedean grids for which it was not known: it is $2/3$ for the truncated hexagonal grid, $3/7$ for the truncated square grid, and $1/3$ for the trihexagonal (kagome) grid, the elongated triangular grid and the snub hexagonal grid. All lower bounds are proved by the discharging method. For the three remaining non-regular Archimedean grids, we also obtain some bounds: the minimum density lies between $3/7$ and $13/30$ for the truncated trihexagonal grid, between $1/3$ and $11/30$ for the rhombitrihexagonal grid, and between $2/7$ and $9/28$ for the snub square grid. As a by-product, we prove that every identifying code of a cubic graph with the slow growth property in which every vertex lies on exactly one triangle (resp. $4$-cycle) has density at least $2/3$ (resp. $3/7$).

papers.title: The Genus-One B-Model Calabi-Yau/Landau-Ginzburg Correspondence
papers.abstract: Let $f:\mathbb C^n\to\mathbb C$ be a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ with an isolated critical point at the origin. The Calabi--Yau/Landau--Ginzburg correspondence predicts a relation between invariants of the Landau--Ginzburg orbifold $(\mathbb C^n/\mathbb Z_n,f)$ and those of the associated Calabi--Yau hypersurface $X_f=\{f=0\}\subset\mathbb{P}^{n-1}$. In this paper, we establish this correspondence for the genus-one B-model. We define the Landau--Ginzburg genus-one B-model invariant intrinsically from the $f$-twisted Laplacian on $\C^n/\Z_n$ as a modification of the torsion-type invariant introduced by Fan and Fang, and prove that it agrees with the corresponding BCOV invariant of $X_f$ up to an additive constant depending only on the dimension. The proof depends on a holomorphic anomaly formula for families of LG models and a uniform estimate for the torsion near a one-node degeneration of $X_f$.
papers.comments: 61 pages. Added a non-probabilistic proof in appendix. Comments and suggestions are welcome!

papers.title: Sharp enumeration and growth of admissible sets of integers
papers.abstract: A set of positive integers is admissible if equal sums of finite subsets always have equal numbers of summands. Let $a(N)$ count the nonempty admissible subsets of $\{1,\ldots,N\}$, and let $b(N)$ count those with maximum $N$. We prove $\log a(N)\sim\log b(N)\simπ\sqrt{2N/3}$, establishing the sharp logarithmic asymptotic proposed by Nicolas. More generally, let $Q_h(N)$ count the subsets for which each integer has subset-sum representations of at most $h$ distinct cardinalities. Uniformly for all positive integers $h,N$, we prove $\log Q_h(N)\asymp\min\{N,\sqrt{hN}\}$ with absolute implied constants. Every infinite set satisfying the same condition for some fixed $h$ has counting function $o(\sqrt x)$. At $h=1$, the uniform count proves the conjecture $\log a(N)\asymp\sqrt N$ of Erdős, Nicolas and Sárközy, and the infinite-set theorem strengthens their conjectured vanishing lower limit to a full limit. The proofs record each subset sum together with its cardinality and use the counting theorem of Campos and the structure theorem of Carpenter, Defant and Kravitz. The sharp count also uses Nicolas's partition enumeration and an elementary construction of a long restricted-sum progression. Finally, we give an exact partition formula and asymptotics for the odd sets with separated alternate cardinality layers suggested by Nicolas, and deduce lower bounds for the number of non-stratified admissible sets.

papers.title: Inductive Grounded Arithmetic: Goodstein, the Hydra, and $Γ_0$
papers.abstract: What does a recursive definition mean in a grounded logic, where a sentence is true only if a terminating process makes it so? This paper takes Kripke's answer for truth, the least fixed point, as a rule. Reflective Grounded Arithmetic (RGA) writes any recursive definition as one self-referential term; Inductive Grounded Arithmetic (IGA) adds the elimination rule for every positive one, making each an inductive definition. IGA is omega-sound and proof-grounded: sound and complete for a semantics whose certificates are its own proofs. IGA proves Goodstein's theorem, the Kirby-Paris hydra game for primitive recursive strategies, and, along Gentzen's route, the consistency of Peano Arithmetic. IGA certifies the Veblen notation below every $\varphi(n,0)$: its accessibility ordinal there is $\varphi(ω,0)$, that of the paracomplete truth theory PKF. Every theorem is machine-checked in Isabelle/HOL; order types and PKF's ordinal are cited. IGA proves the Veblen notation well-founded exactly when it admits bivalence of accessibility for it, which it does not, and that bivalence is sound exactly when the order is well-founded. So $Γ_0$ lies exactly one instance of excluded middle away, and that instance, the well-foundedness sentence and one membership claim in an internal form of Kleene's $\mathcal{O}$ are interderivable over IGA. Bivalence at the Bachmann-Howard order keeps proof-groundedness. One such claim buys well-foundedness of the countable part of Buchholz's notation at every finite level, of type $ψ_0(Ω_ω)$, and $k$ stratified bivalence rules give a proof-grounded system proving the countable part up to level $k$ well-founded; $k$ iterated closings-off of truth do too, sound only for a closed-off model. Unrestricted conditional proof is inconsistent (Curry's paradox); the purchase is implication at a hypothesis not provably decided.

papers.title: A 1.932 Guarantee for (r,Q) Policies in Continuous-Review Lost-Sales Inventory Systems
papers.abstract: We provide a uniform guarantee for a continuous-review lost-sales inventory system with unit Poisson demand, deterministic lead time, and fixed ordering costs: a simple algorithm computes an $(r,Q)$ policy and chooses between that policy and no replenishment, with cost at most $(\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{6})/2<1.932$ times the unrestricted nonanticipative optimum. The algorithm starts by generating an optimal integer base-stock policy, which at zero setup cost achieves the tight worst-case factor $\sqrt{2}$ relative to the optimal system cost. For positive setup costs, it uses the reorder point of this integer base-stock policy and an integer lot at the economic order quantity scale. The inclusion of ordinary base stock in the continuous-review capped base-stock family also improves that family's earlier asymptotic $1.79$ upper guarantee to a uniform $\sqrt{2}$ guarantee valid at every finite parameter vector. To establish these guarantees, we construct a computable lower bound on the zero-setup optimal cost by tracking units already on hand or committed for delivery. We then combine it with a bound on holding and setup costs required by batching to obtain the general-setup guarantee and instance-specific performance bounds for any admissible replenishment policy. In our numerical study, the largest estimated policy-cost-to-lower-bound ratios are about $1.59$ for our heuristic $(r, Q)$ policy and $1.47$ after joint optimization of $r$ and $Q$. The heuristic also performs well against the optimized policy: over the sampled instances, its median extra cost ranges from $2.33\%$ to $3.91\%$, depending on the setup cost.

papers.title: The rank of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes
papers.abstract: The canonical $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-linear Hadamard codes are the Gray images of the $\mathbb{Z}_{2^s}$-additive codes. Their rank, the dimension of the binary linear span, was known in closed form only for $s\le 3$, and for $s \ge 4$ only through computer computations for small lengths. We give a method that computes the rank for every $s$. We show that the rank is a binomial polynomial in the type parameters, with coefficients $ρ_s(\boldsymbol{k})$ independent of the length. We compute all the coefficients for $s\le 5$, which yields explicit rank formulas over $\mathbb{Z}_4$ and $\mathbb{Z}_8$ (recovering the known ones), and over $\mathbb{Z}_{16}$ and $\mathbb{Z}_{32}$.

papers.title: Voevodsky's motives and zeroth slice of motivic sphere
papers.abstract: Let $S$ be a noetherian scheme of finite Krull dimension and let $R$ be a commutative ring in which the positive residue characteristics of $S$ are invertible. We identify Voevodsky's stable Nisnevich category of motives with $R$-coefficients with the category of modules over the zeroth slice of the motivic sphere with derived $R$-coefficients. The equivalence takes the free module on a smooth $S$-scheme to its motive with transfers and commutes with pullback and extension of coefficients. It applies to singular and nonreduced schemes and to mixed-characteristic bases. The main geometric input is the base change stability of Voevodsky's motivic Eilenberg--MacLane spectrum $HR_S$. We prove this using permutation quotients of tori, families of relative cycles and arithmetic power homotopies. The identification over fields and the reconstruction theorem of Cisinski--Déglise then give the module equivalence.

papers.title: Quasi locally free sheaves on primitive double schemes
papers.abstract: Let $X_2$ be a complex primitive double scheme, $X=(X_2)_{red}$. The ideal sheaf of $X$ is a line bundle on $X$. Let $E$ be a coherent sheaf on $X_2$. Then there exists a nonempty open subset $U$ of $X_2$ and integers $m_1$, $m_2$, uniquely determined by $E$, such that $E_{|U}$ is locally isomorphic to $(O_X\otimes C^{m_1})\oplus(O_{X_2}\otimes C^{m_2})$. If we can take $U=X_2$, we say the $E$ is quasi locally free. If $m_1=1$ we say that $E$ is rigid. In this case, we show that deformations of $E$ are of the same type. So locally free sheaves and rigid quasi locally free sheaves on $X_2$ play the same role on $X_2$ as locally free sheaves do on smooth schemes. In this paper we study the existence and description of quasi locally free sheaves, and flat families of such sheaves.

papers.title: Converse symplectic interlacing via low-rank singular value perturbations
papers.abstract: The symplectic interlacing theorem states that the symplectic spectrum of a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix satisfies a $2k$-step interlacing relation with the symplectic spectrum of every $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix. We prove the converse in this paper. More precisely, given a global symplectic spectrum of size $n$ and a local symplectic spectrum of size $n-k$ satisfying the $2k$-step interlacing inequalities, we construct a $2n \times 2n$ real symmetric positive definite matrix having the prescribed global symplectic spectrum and a $2(n-k) \times 2(n-k)$ $s$-principal submatrix of it having the prescribed local symplectic spectrum. A novelty of our method is building a connection between the $s$-principal submatrix problem and low-rank singular value perturbations. We also provide an algorithm to determine a positive definite matrix that realizes the given global and local symplectic spectra. In the context of the Gaussian quantum marginal problem, our result implies that the symplectic interlacing inequalities are not merely necessary conditions on Gaussian marginals, but are also the complete spectral compatibility conditions for the global-versus-local-mode marginal problem.
papers.comments: A new section has been added. It provides an algorithm to construct the realizing matrix. The introduction has been revised to enhance the readability of the paper

papers.title: Morse-Maxwell Theory for Directed Acyclic Graph
papers.abstract: The Maxwell graph of a directed acyclic graph records the extrema of its iterated basin and hill boundaries. Their unweighted counts need not satisfy Morse inequalities, and the reduction can change homology. We assign multiplicities using the reduced homology of lower and upper order links and retain every vertex with nonzero local homology. This modified reduction preserves both hierarchies, the local groups, and the homology of all sublevel and superlevel order complexes. Its Morse numbers satisfy the weak and strong Morse inequalities over any field. We give explicit formulas in low dimensions and for complete layered graphs. We also construct local Morse numbers for path homology and prove agreement with the reachability construction on complete layered graphs, including those without transitive arrows. Counterexamples distinguish the homology theories and show that local Morse degrees need not equal vertex depths. A comparison with discrete-gradient methods explains the role of auxiliary choices.

papers.title: Fast rates for the classification of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths
papers.abstract: In binary classification problems, plug-in classifiers can sometimes achieve faster excess risk rates than the underlying estimation rate. In this work, we study a supervised classification problem based on repeated independent observations of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, with both time-homogeneous and time-inhomogeneous drifts. We show that, under a suitable separation condition on the class-dependent drifts, a plug-in classifier attains an excess risk of quadratic order in the corresponding parametric or nonparametric estimation error. The theoretical approach utilizes the Wiener chaos representation and spectral theory to characterize the log-likelihood ratio as a quadratic form of Gaussian random variables, enabling a precise analysis of margin behaviour and deviation results. This extends the fast-rate results from classification problems with linear discriminant models and Gaussian white noise models to dynamical diffusion systems with Gaussian structure.

papers.title: Computer-Assisted Results for $n$-Sided Non-Transitive Dice Taking Face Values in $[n]$
papers.abstract: We consider non-transitivity among dice with $n$ sides restricted to taking face values in the set $\{1,\ldots,n\}$. We give a computer-assisted proof that $n=6$ is the smallest $n\ge3$ which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length $n$ with uniform and minimal winning advantage. For $n=6$, we identify the two unique non-transitive cycles of length $6$. We present computational evidence supporting a conjecture that $n=6$ is the largest $n\ge3$ which admits a non-transitive cycle of maximum length $n$ with uniform and minimal winning advantage.
papers.comments: 11 pages, revised exposition, supplementary material includes Julia code, fixed metadata tex using $$ rather than \(\)

papers.title: Real-rooted Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomials of crown posets and wheel and whirl matroids
papers.abstract: For every integer $r\ge3$, the crown order polytope on $2r$ elements and the rank-$r$ whirl base polytope have the same Ehrhart $h^*$-polynomial. We also prove that every convex combination of the $h^*$-polynomials of the rank-$r$ wheel and whirl base polytopes has degree $2r-2$ and only simple negative roots. Its coefficients are positive, unimodal, and strictly ultra log-concave of order $2r-2$. These results settle the real-rootedness conjecture of Lundström and Saud Maia Leite for crown order polytopes.

papers.title: Local Smoothing Estimates of a Class of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
papers.abstract: We prove local smoothing estimates for a class of Schrödinger operators on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

papers.title: Exchange graphs and $τ$-tilting complexes of surface rigid algebras
papers.abstract: Let $A=Λ_{\mathbf R}$ be the surface rigid algebra associated with a partial tagged triangulation $\mathbf R$ of a punctured marked surface with nonempty boundary, and let $C_A$ be the Cartan matrix of $A$. We classify the connected components of the support $τ$-tilting graph of $A$. For connected $A$, such a graph is disconnected if and only if $A$ is non-local and weakly symmetric with $\operatorname{rank}C_A=1$. The graph then has exactly two components. The completion graph of every nonzero basic $τ$-rigid pair over connected $A$ is connected. When $\mathbf R$ is nonempty and all arc endpoints are punctures, we construct an explicit homotopy equivalence from the realization of the support $τ$-tilting complex to a sphere of dimension $\operatorname{rank}C_A-1$. Under the same hypothesis, $A$ is $τ$-tilting finite if and only if $C_A$ is positive definite. In the finite case, we give a root-system realization of the $g$-vectors of indecomposable $τ$-rigid pairs, with types $A$, $D$ and $C$ determined by the tagged surface configuration.
papers.comments: 42 pages, 5 figures; added results on spherical homotopy types; revised exposition and title

papers.title: Brownian Convex Hulls in Arbitrary Dimension: Absorption and Intersection Probabilities
papers.abstract: For every $d\ge1$, we determine prescribed-point absorption probabilities for the convex hulls of standard Brownian motion and Brownian bridges in $\mathbb R^d$, obtaining explicit one-dimensional integral formulas involving standard special functions. For example, in dimension three the Brownian-motion absorption probability for a point at distance $r>0$ from the origin is \[ p_3^B(r)=\frac{r}{\sqrt2\,π^{3/2}}\int_0^\infty\left(\fracπ{2\sqrt{1+v^2}}-1\right)\mathrm{e}^{-r^2(1+v^2)/4}(K_1-K_0)\!\left(\frac{r^2(1+v^2)}4\right)\,\mathrm{d}v, \] where $K_ν$ denotes the modified Bessel function of the second kind. For fixed $d$, the non-absorption probabilities of a prescribed nonzero point by Brownian-motion and Brownian-bridge hulls over $[0,T]$ are asymptotic to explicit positive constants times $T^{-1/2}(\log T)^{d-1}$ and $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$, respectively, as $T\to\infty$. We determine the Mellin and Laplace transforms of the first time $τ_d$ a Brownian-motion hull absorbs a prescribed point at unit distance. In high dimensions, both $τ_d$ and the time $τ_d^{\mathrm{ball}}$ to absorb the entire unit ball satisfy the same central limit theorem: \[ \frac{\logτ_d-2d}{2\sqrt d}\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1),\qquad\frac{\logτ_d^{\mathrm{ball}}-2d}{2\sqrt d}\xrightarrow{\mathrm d}N(0,1), \qquad d\to\infty.\] Thus both times have leading exponential scale $\mathrm{e}^{2d}$. For Brownian bridges, prescribed-point and unit-ball absorption also exhibit the same Gaussian transition, but on the shorter scale $\mathrm{e}^d$. For two independent Brownian motions started one unit apart, we show that the non-intersection probability of their convex hulls is of order $T^{-1}(\log T)^{d-1}$ for fixed $d$ and large $T$. In high dimensions, the first intersection time has leading exponential scale $\mathrm{e}^d$, and its logarithm satisfies a central limit theorem.
papers.comments: 45 pages. Compared with the previous version, we have added results on intersections of two independent Brownian convex hulls and on high-dimensional absorption by Brownian bridges, and strengthened the high-dimensional result for the unit-ball absorption time to a central limit theorem

papers.title: Newtonian Dynamics in Metric Spaces
papers.abstract: We develop a variational framework for second-order, frictionless (Newtonian) dynamics in metric spaces, extending the metric theory of curves of maximal slope from gradient flows to evolutions with inertia. The construction rests on three pillars, mirroring the first-order theory. First, we introduce a class of second-order absolutely continuous curves, characterized by a geometric--variational inequality on families of tangent geodesics, and define a metric notion of acceleration. Second, we define curves of Newtonian motion as the curves achieving equality in an energy inequality involving an upper gradient--Hessian pair, which in Hilbert spaces is equivalent to Newton's equation $\ddotγ= -\nabla E(γ)$. Third, we propose a two-step predictor--corrector minimizing movement scheme and show that its discrete interpolants satisfy approximate versions of these inequalities. Under extendability and interceptor conditions on geodesics---which are satisfied, for instance, by geodesically uniformly complete, locally compact spaces with curvature bounded below---and under suitable regularity assumptions on the energy, we prove that the scheme converges, up to subsequences, to a curve of Newtonian motion. As an illustration, we recover the linear wave equation as a curve of Newtonian motion driven by the Dirichlet energy. This paper is complemented by the companion paper [Fornasier, Klemenc, Scagliotti, "A Lions Lift Framework for Gradient and Newtonian Evolutions in Wasserstein spaces"], which specifies and adapts the results to the Wasserstein metric space $(\mathcal{P}_2,W_2)$ through Lions lift, which explains Vlasov equations as Newtonian flows on spaces of probability measures.

papers.title: Deterministic Principal-Ideal Responses of Random Operators
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a random compact operator for which each fixed compact shift $X+B$ generates an almost surely deterministic principal ideal. We show that all these ideals are determined by one ideal and one coset. The ideal is generated almost surely by the difference of independent copies of $X$, and the coset consists of all minimizing shifts. For alternating quadratic evaluations under two-sided curvature bounds, the spatial and kernel spectra determine the least ideal and the covariance determines the coset. With the spatial weights and a trace-class skew kernel fixed, the attainable raw ideals fill an explicit order interval. Every ideal in the interval occurs with standard Gaussian row marginals and joint covariance arbitrarily close to the identity. For finite-dimensional operator spaces with infinite-rank coefficient ideal we characterize almost-everywhere saturation in every translate by a spectral summability criterion. For independent Gaussian rows we also compute the least ideal attainable after observing a noise subspace. For Wiener area, finitely many fixed Hilbert-valued temporal integrals leave this ideal unchanged.

papers.title: On the Irreducibility of Locally Analytic Vectors in Certain Banach Representations of $D^\times$
papers.abstract: We investigate the structure of locally analytic representations of $p$-adic groups, and establish a sufficient condition for the irreducibility of locally analytic vectors in certain Banach representations of $D^\times$, where $D$ is the quaternion division algebra over $\mathbb{Q}_p$. As an application, we prove that $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{\mathrm{an}}/\mathrm{JL}(ρ)^{1\text{-}\mathrm{alg}}$ is a topologically irreducible locally analytic representation of $D^\times$ under certain genericity conditions on $ρ$. Here $\mathrm{JL}(ρ)$ is the $ρ(-1)$-multiplicity space in the image of $Π(ρ)$ under Scholze's functor, and $Π(ρ)$ is the representation associated to $ρ$ by the $p$-adic local Langlands correspondence.

papers.title: Monochromatic arm exponents for critical planar percolation
papers.abstract: We determine the monochromatic three-arm exponent for critical planar percolation through the exact spectral threshold of an explicit positive integral operator family with elementary kernels, obtaining $ξ_3=0.76928375\cdots$. Unlike the monochromatic two-arm (backbone) event, the three-arm event can be obstructed by two distinct white clusters, so a Markovian exploration must retain the past connections. We introduce a two-point boundary observable that records these connections. Using the coupling between conformal loop ensemble (CLE) and Liouville quantum gravity (LQG), this observable satisfies a renewal equation in terms of quantum boundary lengths, and yields the explicit operator whose spectral information determines $ξ_3$. Our approach also gives an explicit spectral characterization of monochromatic $n$-arm exponents for all $n\ge4$.
papers.comments: 41 pages, 5 figures. Added a reference to recent numerical results by Wang, Deng, and Li

papers.title: Perfect Forms and Torsion Bounds in Algebraic $K$-Theory over Totally Real and CM Fields
papers.abstract: We extend the method of van Woerden to totally real and CM number fields to obtain an upper bound for the number of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_F)$-equivalence classes of perfect forms. Moreover, by considering appropriate barycentric subdivisions of the Voronoi tessellation, we extend these estimates to the number of $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O}_F)$-orbits of $k$-dimensional faces of the Voronoi tessellation. As a consequence, we improve the asymptotic order of the bounds for the torsion part of $K_m(\mathcal{O}_F)$ obtained by Soulé and Bayer-Fluckiger, Emery, and Houriet. We emphasise the improvement of the general bound for $F=\mathbb{Q}$, unchanged since Soulé's work, and the independence of the discriminant exponent from the field degree for totally real and CM fields.

papers.title: How many sorted projections determine any n points in k dimensions?
papers.abstract: Let $d_1,\dots,d_m$ be directions in $\mathbb{R}^k$, where $k\ge 2$. A multiset $X$ of $n$ points of $\mathbb{R}^k$ projects to the $m$ multisets of numbers $\{\{x\cdot d_j : x\in X\}\}$, or equivalently to the $m$ sorted lists of these numbers. How many directions are needed for these projections to determine every multiset of $n$ points? Two simple bounds are known in every dimension: more than $(k-1)\log_2 n$ directions are always needed, and $(k-1)n+1$ directions in general position always suffice. In the plane much more is known: Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron showed that almost every choice of $O(\log n \log\log n)$ directions suffices. Whether anything similar holds in higher dimensions was left open by Dym, Wellershoff, Tsoukanis, Levy and Balan. We observe that two lemmas of Hair and Sahai, proved for list recovery of random linear codes, answer that question, and by tightening their argument we show that in every dimension almost every choice of $(4k-2)\ln(2n)\ln(k\log_2 2n)+k+1$ directions suffices. For $k\le 10$ this beats the linear bound once $n$ is larger than about 100: for example, 144 directions suffice for multisets of 1000 points in the plane, and an exact computation lowers this to 133. Letting some of the random blocks in their argument fail removes a factor $\log k$: almost every choice of $O(k\log n\log\log n)$ directions suffices, uniformly in $k$ and $n$. We also show that $2k-1$ directions never determine three points, so that the logarithmic lower bound is not tight; that every $m$ directions in the plane fail on some pair of multisets of size $O(1.65^m)$, improving the bound $O(1.80^m)$ of Matousek, Privetivy and Skovron; and that for each $k$, $m$ and $n$, either almost every choice of $m$ directions works or almost none does.
papers.comments: 33 pages, 9 figures. v2: added word "any" to title, improved a bound following comment from ZM26, added three small special cases, removed unicode from an anc file, and added a statement about deep sets. v3: no new results, but many small text edits for clarity, and also added appendix with four new figures to aid in indexation of results

papers.title: Constrained Mean Variance Portfolio Selection under Reflected Factor Dynamics: Stochastic Riccati Equations, Neumann Problems,and a Deep Solver
papers.abstract: We study extended stochastic Riccati equations (ESREs) arising in constrained continuous time mean variance portfolio selection with random market coefficients. Reflected Markovian diffusions are introduced to model factor dynamics in a bounded state space, naturally leading to homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. A logarithmic transformation converts the extended stochastic Riccati equations into quadratic backward stochastic differential equations (BSDEs) driven by the reflected factors. We establish their probabilistic representation through semilinear parabolic Neumann problems and prove existence and uniqueness of bounded continuous viscosity solutions. Existence is obtained through stability and comparison arguments for quadratic BSDEs, whereas uniqueness is established by combining a Kobylanski-type transformation with a viscosity comparison principle adapted to the Neumann boundary setting. We further develop a Deep BSDE method combining reflected-path simulation, geometry-aware boundary treatment, and efficient evaluation of the constrained Hamiltonian. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of the method, providing a mesh-free framework for high-dimensional constrained portfolio problems with Neumann boundary.

papers.title: Funnel MPC for port-Hamiltonian systems
papers.abstract: Port-Hamiltonian systems are an energy-based modelling formalism, that has strong ties to the physical models and allows interconnection of systems. Funnel MPC, a Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, allows for output tracking with prescribed error bounds. Earlier works focused on systems with stable internal dynamics, which typically excludes port-Hamiltonian systems. We introduce a modified stage cost design that takes into account the port-Hamiltonian structure of the system and allows deactivation of the funnel cost. We show initial and recursive feasibility for a class of port-Hamiltonian systems with relative degree one including unstable internal dynamics.

papers.title: Optimal domains of Volterra-type operators on Bergman spaces
papers.abstract: We consider bounded Volterra-type operators $T_g$ from the weighted Bergman space $A^q_β$ to $A^p_α$. The holomorphic optimal domain $[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is introduced and shown to be a quasi-Banach space. We show that the intersection of the optimal domains is equal to $A^q_β$ if $p\le q$, while if $p>q$, it is strictly larger than $A^q_β$. Moreover, $A^q_β \subsetneq[T_{g},A^p_α]$ is established for $p\neq q$. If $p=q$, by contrast, $A^p_β$ may coincide with $[T_{g},A^p_α]$. The multiplier algebras and strict inclusions with respect to varying parameters are established. For example, we determine exactly when $[T_{g},A^s_γ] \subset [T_{g},A^p_α]$ for some $g\in \operatorname{Hol}(\mathbb{D})$. We further study the set $V_g^p$ and characterize the coincidence of the holomorphic optimal domains.

papers.title: Euclidean Hulls of Double Cyclic Codes of Arbitrary Block Lengths
papers.abstract: A $\mathbb{Z}_2$-double cyclic code of block length $(r,s)$ can be viewed as a $\mathbb{Z}_2[x]$-submodule of $\mathbb{Z}_2[x]/\langle x^r - 1 \rangle \times \mathbb{Z}_2[x]/\langle x^s - 1 \rangle$. In 2023, Gao et al. \cite{GWF23} investigated the Euclidean hulls of double cyclic codes over $\mathbb{Z}_2$ for both separable and non-separable cases. In the non-separable setting, they determined the hull generators under the assumption that the block lengths are coprime (i.e., $\gcd(r,s)=1$) and left the non-coprime case ($\gcd(r,s) > 1$) as an open problem. In this paper, we resolve this open problem by deriving the explicit hull generators for arbitrary block lengths $(r,s)$, recovering the coprime setting as a special case of our framework. Furthermore, we establish the necessary and sufficient conditions for non-separable double cyclic codes to be linear complementary dual (LCD) and provide several numerical examples to validate our theoretical findings.

papers.title: Rotating Walks, Derandomized Squares, and Permutation Conjugated Walks
papers.abstract: Using the recent strong convergence results of Bordenave and Collins (Annals of Mathematics) and Chen et al. (Annals of Mathematics), we study the average case behavior of rotating random walks of Cohen and Maor (STOC 2023) and the derandomized square construction of Rozenman and Vadhan (RANDOM 2005). Concretely, we prove a conjecture of Cohen et al. (ITCS 2025) regarding the average case behavior of derandomized squaring for random graphs and show that the existential bounds of Cohen and Maor for their rotating random walk construction hold with high-probability for random graphs. Using the results of O'Donnell and Wu (FOCS 2020), we can in polynomial time construct a family of graphs and rotations which almost saturate the bounds of Cohen and Maor, and meet the bounds conjectured by Cohen et al. for all vertex-transitive auxiliary graphs of fixed degree in the derandomized square. Finally, we study independent random permutation conjugates of deterministic regular graph adjacency matrices. We prove quantitative weak convergence to freely independent tree adjacency operators when the degrees are fixed and the girths tend to infinity. Separately, a covering argument gives deterministic spectral lower bounds for polynomials with non-negative coefficients, recovering the lower bound of Cohen et al. for rotating walks.

papers.title: Another Multivector Inverse Algorithm
papers.abstract: A numerical algorithm is described for computing the inverse of a non-singular multivector across dimensions. The method wraps a reversion-like product around a Faddeev--LeVerrier--Souriau (FLS) polynomial core. While FLS provides dimensional extensibility, the wrapper reduces the polynomial order of the FLS method, and introduces a sparse multivector which can be further exploited. The construction and essential properties of the initial involution are explained. For dimensions 4--7, the optimized inverse requires fewer real multiplications than a same-dimension multivector product. Dimensions 8--11 follow easily on common hardware with similar efficiency. For dimensions 12--15, higher-precision arithmetic demonstrates the generality of the algorithm when the arithmetic can support it. Performance on common hardware is reported. Directions are included for obtaining a Python package with examples for numerical computation in Clifford algebra, supporting arbitrary signatures including degenerate cases.
papers.comments: 17 pages, 1 figure. To be included in the conference proceedings for AGACSE 2026

papers.title: A Diophantine definition of $\mathbb{Z}$ in $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that $\mathbb{Z}$ is a Diophantine subset of $\mathbb{Q}$. More precisely, there exist an integer $m\ge 1$ and a polynomial of total degree at most four in $m+1$ variables whose rational zero set projects onto $\mathbb{Z}$ under the first coordinate. We construct a Diophantine model of $\mathbb{Z}$ on an elliptic curve and use it to define real intervals with rational endpoints, each containing an integer. A denominator bound identifies a rational number in a sufficiently short interval with that integer. The key ingredients are a criterion for square denominators, obtained using the Tian--Yuan--Zhang genus-point criterion for congruent number elliptic curves, and a height bound from quaternionic abelian surfaces. The Green--Tao theorem supplies prime progressions needed to define squaring, and hence multiplication, in the model. Our proof is inspired by OpenAI's approach to Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Q}$, but does not rely on the $2$-converse or $2$-adic Fontaine--Mazur results announced and invoked by OpenAI.
papers.comments: A substantially shorter realisation of the original strategy, incorporating Manjul Bhargava's ideas

papers.title: Counting Second-Order Schreier Sets with Minimum 2
papers.abstract: A finite nonempty subset of the positive integers is first-order Schreier if the minimum element of that set is greater than or equal to the size of the set. A nonempty subset of the positive integers $X$ is second-order Schreier if $X$ is a union of $d$ first-order Schreier sets for some $d \leq \min X$. We study a combinatorial relationship between the count of second-order Schreier sets and the Fibonacci sequence. Specifically, we show that the second-order Schreier set with minimum $2$ and maximum $n+4$ is one more than the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the convolution of the Fibonacci numbers $(F_1, F_2, \ldots)$ with $(F_2, F_3, \ldots)$ (given by Sequence A023610 in the OEIS).

papers.title: Asymptotic efficiency of tests for quantum statistical models
papers.abstract: In classical statistics, local asymptotic normality provides a general framework for characterizing optimal testing power and constructing asymptotically efficient procedures. Extending this framework to quantum statistical models introduces additional challenges arising from the noncommutativity of observables and the need to optimize over quantum measurements. In this paper, we develop a theory of asymptotic efficiency for quantum hypothesis testing using quantum local asymptotic normality and the asymptotic representation theorem. We establish sharp nuisance-maximin power bounds for one-sided tests and two-sided tests within the unbiased class by reducing the corresponding classical--quantum Gaussian shift experiments to classical testing problems. This reduction is justified through a quantum Hunt--Stein argument that accommodates both commuting and noncommuting Gaussian coordinates. Under suitable asymptotic invariance conditions, the resulting bounds transfer to the original quantum experiments and are attained by scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests. We further develop a two-stage adaptive construction that achieves the same local asymptotic power without knowledge of the reference parameter. As an application, we study testing of smooth spectral functionals of quantum states. We compare scalar symmetric logarithmic derivative tests with the weak Schur sampling plug-in test and with optimally weighted linear statistics of its fluctuations. This comparison distinguishes loss from the plug-in weighting from a gap between the best such spectral statistic and the scalar score procedure. We characterize equality of the corresponding variances and illustrate the two gaps through explicit examples.

papers.title: The Dirichlet problem for sum Hessian equations on uniformly $(k-1)$-convex domains
papers.abstract: In this paper, we mainly study the sum Hessian equation with general boundary values in the case $2\leq k\leq n$. Under the conditions that the boundary is uniformly $(k-1)$-convex, the right-hand side is monotone non-decreasing in $u$, convex in the gradient, and has a suitably small linear gradient growth, we prove the existence of a unique smooth admissible solution. The proof constructs the global subsolution and gradient barriers by using strictly $k$-convex function, and derives the boundary second-order estimates from the tangential linearizations and a duality inequality for the boundary curvature.

papers.title: Strictly pseudoconvex $CR$ structures on $\sfS^5$ that can be turned inside out
papers.abstract: The existence of a complex structure on $\sfS^{6}$ implies that of strictlty pseudoconvex structures on $\sfS^{5}$ which can be turned inside out by a homotopy.

papers.title: Finite sums of weighted composition operators on the Fock space
papers.abstract: We study finite sums of weighted composition operators on the classical Fock space. We show that no cancellation phenomenon occurs when the composition symbols are pairwise distinct: such a sum is bounded, compact, or belongs to the Schatten class S_p, 0<p<\infty, if and only if each summand has the corresponding property. We also obtain two-sided essential norm estimates and quantitative Schatten norm comparisons for fixed distinct nonconstant symbols. As an application, we obtain corresponding boundedness, compactness, and Schatten-class results for finite sums of generalized Volterra-type integral operators.

papers.title: Decision-Weighted Limit Theorems: Less Conservative Robust Optimization
papers.abstract: Limit theorems provide a natural way to construct tractable models for optimization under uncertainty. Existing approaches typically apply them to unweighted sums of uncertain parameters and use the resulting bounds to construct uncertainty sets. We show that sharper formulations are obtained by applying limit theorems directly to the uncertain linear expressions in the optimization problem, with the decision variables as weights. For independent random variables with finite variance, the weighted central limit theorem yields a second-order cone constraint with a decision-dependent protection term, and for heavy-tailed random variables governed by stable limit laws, the weighted approach yields power-cone constraints. Using norm duality, we show that, under a condition on the individual bounds, the feasible region of the unweighted formulation is contained in that of the weighted one. In 16,000 knapsack instances with a prescribed violation probability of 5%, the weighted formulation improves the optimal objective value by 20.9% on average, with overall average violation probabilities between 3.45% and 4.95%, whereas those of the unweighted formulation are near zero.

papers.title: Hyperkähler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
papers.abstract: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $α$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $σ$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $π:\mathscr M\toΛ_0$ where $Λ_0$ encodes the admissible pairs $(α,σ)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in $Λ_0$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(α,σ)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$. For the four-dimensional moduli spaces of types $E_6,E_7,E_8$, we compute these classes to get explicit formulas for the period maps.

papers.title: A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
papers.abstract: We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

papers.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
papers.abstract: A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved. However, very few results are known for graphs with maximum degree four or more. Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana showed that every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{19})$-packing edge-coloring and a $(1^2,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. In this paper, we improve the results of Henderson, Kennedy, and Santana by showing every graph with degree at most four has a $(1,2^{17})$-packing edge-coloring. As a corollary of our result, every graph with degree at most four has a $(1^2,2^{16})$-packing edge-coloring.

papers.title: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
papers.abstract: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A. Hanlon, J. Hicks, and O. Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

papers.title: A Two-Spectrum Deterministic Equivalent for Random Skew-Kernel Matrices
papers.abstract: Rank-one perturbations of the mean characteristic polynomial of a random skew-kernel matrix assign a positive spatial weight to each root. For independent centered isotropic rows, the resulting response tracks the sample almost surely against each deterministic spatial test, uniformly over positive scales and arbitrary inputs, exactly when row energies concentrate on common projections of proportional rank. Directional absolute first moments determine this condition. The determinant Jensen gap controls the spatial response in every real orthonormal basis. For identity spatial covariance, logarithmic derivatives of the mean determinant give the temporal weights of the row energies it detects. Flat kernels of one prescribed rank suffice to test the row condition. A scalar equation in the two input spectra approximates the matrix response of the roots within $4/d$ in normalized trace norm. A varying ordinary response and the same-scale overlap of independent samples recover both input laws up to reciprocal rescaling, with Lipschitz stability of the relative spatial parameter and an optimal logarithmic modulus for the compactified laws on intervals of positive variation. Brownian area gives explicit spatial half-Cauchy mixtures.

papers.title: Global genetic inference at the scale of mass disasters
papers.abstract: DNA-based disaster victim identification is commonly performed sequentially, with matches accepted before all genetic evidence is considered jointly. However, early matches may be incorrect or inconsistent with the globally most likely assignment, and treating them as final can affect subsequent identifications. Joint analysis avoids this dependence on decision order, but combinatorial growth has historically made it prohibitive in large cases. In this paper, we show that the general joint identification problem is NP-hard and develop a local-to-global framework for joint genetic inference at scale. We reduce the search using genetic compatibility tests, likelihood-based pruning of unlikely assignments, and symmetry reductions. We represent pedigree likelihoods as polynomials and reformulate the Elston-Stewart algorithm for efficient parallel likelihood evaluation on GPUs. Together, these advances yield a manageable set of candidate assignments and their likelihoods, from which we construct an integer linear program that resolves competing identifications and determines the global maximum-likelihood assignment. In small benchmarks, the method recovers the exhaustive-search optimum with up to 99.96% fewer likelihood evaluations. We also apply it to simulated disasters involving up to 10 thousand victims and missing persons. The framework is not limited to a single global optimum but yields a list of probable alternative assignments, thus providing a flexible tool to be used alongside other forensic evidence.

papers.title: On the $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic
papers.abstract: This paper gives a new path to determine all $\mathbb{F}_q$-linear relations among multiple zeta values in positive characteristic, which had been done by Huang, Lai, Li and the author. The path used in this paper is based on the idea of operator generation, which originated from the work of Todd, developed by the author, and independently by Im-Kim-Ngo Dac.

papers.title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
papers.abstract: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S. We prove the Ramsey Theorem for Edge Ideals: For any betti number indices i,j, and any number of colors m, there is a graph F such that for every m-coloring of the edges of F, there is a color l such that beta_{i,j}(S/I_{F_l}) >0, where F_l is the subgraph of F whose edges are in color l. Moreover, the number of vertices of F is at most jm^2.
papers.comments: 12 pages. Two typos in the proof of Theorem 5 removed

papers.title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
papers.abstract: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jordán: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

papers.title: A Complete Classification of the One-Dimensional Nonlocal Eigenvalue Problem
papers.abstract: We give a complete classification of the spectral stability of the following one-dimensional nonlocal eigenvalue problem (NLEP) $$ \partial_x^2φ-φ+pw^{p-1}φ-γ(p-1)\frac{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^{r-1}φdx}{\int_{\mathbb{R}}w^r dx}w^p=λφ, $$ where $w$ is the unique positive even solution of $w''-w+w^p=0$ decaying at infinity, $p,r>1$, and $γ\in\mathbb{C}$ with $\Reγ\ge0$. This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. When $r<(p+3)/2$, the arcs open to the right, and the strictly stable region lies between them. Their common endpoint is $γ=1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ=γ_H>1$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$. In each case, the two arcs approach a common vertical asymptote. As an application, for real $γ\ge0$, the condition for strict spectral stability is $γ>1$ when $r\ge(p-1)/2$ and $γ>γ_H$ when $1<r<(p-1)/2$, where $γ_H>1$ is the value at which a conjugate pair of eigenvalues crosses the imaginary axis. The key ingredient in determining how the number of eigenvalues in the open right half-plane changes at imaginary-axis crossings is a cumulative estimate for the mixed-sign spectral weights that arise for certain $p$ and $r$ with $1<p<3$ and $1<r<2$.

papers.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
papers.abstract: Let $X\to C$ be a projective fibration over a curve over a global field. We prove a height inequality for relatively nef adelic line bundles on $X$ whose underlying line bundles are nef. For a nef, relatively ample line bundle over a finitely generated field, we deduce a lower bound for the local energy at almost every complex or nonarchimedean realization of a fixed polarized model. Over $\mathbb C$, for an ample line bundle and a smooth positive polarization, the Euler--Lagrange equation is the Calabi--Yau equation. On the projective bundle of a vector bundle of degree zero, our energy on quotient metrics agrees with Donaldson's functional when the determinant metric is fixed. We propose a construction of canonical heights on parameter spaces using envelopes of local energies.

papers.title: The Schoen-Yau-Schick Obstruction in All Dimensions
papers.abstract: We prove that closed Schoen--Yau--Schick manifolds admit no metric of positive scalar curvature in all dimensions. Building on the singular dimension descent of Bi--Zhu, we extend their topological argument from overtorical manifolds to the Schoen--Yau--Schick setting. The key is to detect a non-spherical two-dimensional homology class by a cohomology class with finite coefficients and preserve the resulting nonzero degree throughout the descent, leading to a contradiction on the terminal surface.
papers.comments: 25 pages, 2 figures. v2: Added an AI use statement. Comments are welcome!

papers.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
papers.abstract: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. Bérczi and Fehér conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient. We prove that generalized Bernoulli polynomials of real order at least their degree have simple real zeros. Applied to the shifted quotient, this gives strict ultra-log-concavity in the Schur index at every positive shift. For the original Newton coefficients, we establish strict log-concavity with an explicit multiplicative margin in two uniform regions. A Hahn projection gives a square-root band about the balanced Schur index; a complex saddle estimate extends this to a band of linear width. Uniform estimates for the cumulants of a normalized Schur functional give a terminal Newton region of linear width. Polynomial coefficient identities also establish every row with Schur index at most six or imbalance at most nine. The argument separates log-concavity in the Schur, derivative and Newton indices and identifies the factorial factors in the transfer between the latter two. The unrestricted Newton log-concavity conjecture remains open.

papers.title: Regularity and stabilization of integral closures of powers of homogeneous ideals
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish explicit polynomial bounds for the regularity defect and the stabilization index of integral closures of powers of arbitrary homogeneous ideals over fields of any characteristic. Specifically, let $I \subseteq K[x_{1}, \dots, x_{n}]$ be a nonzero proper homogeneous ideal generated in degrees at most $d$. We prove that $\reg \overline{I^{s}} \le ρ(I)s + d^{(n-1)2^{n}}$ for every $s \ge 1$, where $ρ(I) \le d$ denotes the eventual slope of $\reg \overline{I^{s}}$. Furthermore, the stabilization bound is polynomial in $d$ for a fixed number of variables $n$. In characteristic zero, an upper bound for the first Hilbert coefficient yields a significantly sharper exponent. Our approach relies on exact equigenerated reductions, free lattice constructions within normalized Rees algebras, monic Frobenius presentations, and Tor-module regularity controls, complemented by generic source hyperplanes that reduce the stabilization behavior to the eventual nonvanishing of graded components.

papers.title: Electric combined-field-only P1 Galerkin BEM for PEC scattering with scalar Helmholtz operators
papers.abstract: We develop a Galerkin boundary element method for the indirect electric combined-field-only integral equation (ECFOIE) for perfectly electrically conducting obstacles with smooth surfaces. The method is free of low-frequency breakdown and of spurious resonances. It applies scalar Helmholtz operators componentwise, so that fast scalar solvers can be reused, with less memory than a Rao-Wilton-Glisson (RWG) discretization. The iteration count of the Calderón-regularized ECFOIE (R-ECFOIE) is constant under mesh refinement and, with a complex-wavenumber Calderón regularizer, grows only mildly with frequency. The discretization uses continuous, nodal piecewise-linear basis functions on flat triangular meshes, with essentially as many unknowns as an RWG discretization, and tangential and normal projections and the mean curvature of the obstacle's surface carry the vector structure. On flat meshes the curvature is concentrated on the edges, and we average the edge measure obtained from the first variation of area over vertex patches, which gives sparse curvature matrices. At low frequency, four Lagrange-multiplier constraints on the induced charge and on the longitudinal dipole moments of the far field keep the R-ECFOIE accurate in the quasi-static regime, tested on scatterers eight orders of magnitude smaller than the wavelength. Under mesh refinement, the errors decrease at about second order. A Helmholtz resonator, a rounded Fichera cube, and a smoothed Stanford bunny are compared with electric field integral equation (EFIE) solutions, and the first two also with electrostatic references at extreme low frequency.

papers.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
papers.abstract: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. We disprove this conjecture for every exponent $n=2k$ with $k\ge3$ odd. For each such $n$, we prove that $D(C_n^r)>r(n-1)+1$ for every $r\ge 8n-7$.

papers.title: Higher-order estimates for $p$-harmonic functions in the plane
papers.abstract: Closing a longstanding gap in the theory, we establish uniform interior $C^{k,β}$ estimates for planar $p$-harmonic functions with $1<p<2$. These estimates hold for every integer $k\ge2$ and every $0<β<1$ such that $k+β<s(p)$, where $s(p)$ is the optimal regularity order identified by Iwaniec and Manfredi. As consequences, we obtain decay estimates at critical points, a Liouville theorem with optimal growth exponent, and uniform higher-order estimates for the flux of planar $q$-harmonic functions with $q>2$.
papers.comments: The Lean code and a description of the formalization process are available at https://github.com/na0b/phigherorder-lean

papers.title: Cameron--Martin theorem for SLE welding measures
papers.abstract: For $κ\in(0,4]$, we prove a Cameron--Martin theorem for the welding law induced by SLE$_κ$ loop measure. Under simultaneous left and right composition $h\mapsto\varphi\circ h\circψ^{-1}$, the transformed law is mutually absolutely continuous with respect to the original law exactly when both maps belong to the Weil--Petersson group, and is mutually singular otherwise. Thus the Weil--Petersson group is the quasi-invariance group of the welding law under composition on either side. We also prove that it is its own normalizer in the group of orientation-preserving circle homeomorphisms. For Weil--Petersson pairs, we derive an explicit Radon--Nikodym derivative in terms of a relative action well defined for SLE weldings and prove that it belongs to $L^{1+\varepsilon}$ for some $\varepsilon>0$ depending on the pair.

papers.title: Nonabelian mirrors and Gromov-Witten invariants
papers.abstract: We propose quantum differential equations (QDEs) for periods of nonabelian mirror theories and develop an algorithm for constructing them directly from the mirrors. We verify the proposal by recovering known quantum differential equations of Grassmannians and Picard-Fuchs equations of Calabi-Yau complete intersections in Grassmannians. Our algorithm applies to a broad class of nonabelian GLSMs and yields new examples of quantum differential equations for several Fano varieties. The associated cohomology-valued generating functions can be extracted directly from these equations. Using them, we compute instanton numbers of both complete-intersection and non-complete-intersection Calabi-Yau manifolds, including the Pfaffian and Gulliksen--Negård Calabi-Yau threefolds. The resulting instanton numbers agree with all previously known computations, while the generating functions obtained for the non-complete-intersection examples are new.
papers.comments: V2: 79 pages, 1 figure. Compared with the first arXiv version, numerous typos have been corrected, terminology clarified, and the presentation improved. AI was used for proofreading at the final stage and also provided a technical suggestion that was incorporated into the revision. See the Statement of AI Usage for details. The main results and conclusions remain unchanged

papers.title: Active Learning For Contextual Linear Optimization: A Margin-Based Approach
papers.abstract: We develop the first active learning method for contextual linear optimization. Specifically, we introduce a label acquisition algorithm that sequentially decides whether to request the ``labels'' of feature samples arriving in an unlabeled data stream, where the labels correspond to the objective coefficients in the linear optimization problem. The label acquisition rule is guided by the decision loss induced by the predicted coefficients, known as the Smart Predict-then-Optimize (SPO) loss. Motivated by the structure of the SPO loss, our algorithm uses the distance to degeneracy as a margin-based criterion for label acquisition. The algorithm processes incoming feature samples in batches, acquiring within each batch only the labels of samples whose distance to degeneracy falls below a rejection threshold. We derive non-asymptotic bounds for direct SPO-loss minimization over a general hypothesis class and for surrogate-loss minimization over a linear prediction class. These bounds demonstrate that, under certain natural conditions, our margin-based active learning algorithm requires fewer labels than supervised learning to achieve the same excess population risk for the chosen training loss. We provide concrete examples in which these conditions hold under continuous (sub-)Gaussian noise. Finally, we present numerical evidence demonstrating the practical value of our approach in applications such as personalized pricing and shortest-path problems.

papers.title: Symmetries, correlation functions, and entanglement of general quantum Motzkin spin-chains
papers.abstract: Motzkin spin-chains, which include `colorless' (integer spin $s=1$) and `colorful' ($s \geq 2$) variants, are one-dimensional (1D) local integer spin models notable for their lack of a conformal field theory (CFT) description of their low-energy physics, despite being gapless. The colorful variants are particularly unusual, as they exhibit power-law violation of the area-law of entanglement entropy (as $\sqrt{n}$ in system size $n$), rather than a logarithmic violation as seen in a CFT. In this work, we analytically discover several unique properties of these models, potentially suggesting a new universality class for their low-energy physics. We identify a complex structure of symmetries and unexpected scaling behavior in spin-spin correlations, which deviate from known 1D universality classes. Specifically, the $s=1$ chain exhibits $U(1)$ spontaneous symmetry breaking and ferromagnetic order. Meanwhile, the $s \geq 2$ chains do not appear to spontaneously break any symmetries, but display quasi-long-range algebraic order with power-law decaying correlations, inconsistent with standard Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) critical exponents. We also derive asymptotic scaling expressions, with explicit additive constants, for entanglement measures in both colorless and colorful chains, generalizing previous results of Movassagh [J. Math Phys. (2017)], while providing benchmarks for potential quantum simulation experiments. The $\sqrt{n}$ entanglement scaling implies that any matrix-product-state description of these ground states requires bond dimension $e^{Ω(\sqrt{n})}$; this superpolynomial cost of the standard 1D tensor-network toolkit, along with the analytical tractability of their ground state properties, positions Motzkin spin chains as intriguing testbeds for quantum simulation of many-body physics.

papers.title: Fast Mixed-Precision Real Evaluation
papers.abstract: Evaluating real numbers to high precision is important in computational science, numerical computing, and in hardware and software design. Efficient algorithms exist for computing arithmetic operations and common elementary functions, but composing these primitives into larger expressions remains a challenge. The typical expression-evaluation algorithm computes all primitives in the expression to a uniform precision, doubling that precision until a sufficiently-accurate result is achieved. This is wasteful: usually only a few operations really need to be performed at high precision, and the bulk of the expression could be computed at a much lower, faster precision. However, no rigorous algorithm currently exists to compute these non-uniform precision assignments, nor to leverage non-uniform precision to reduce the number of primitive computations needed to evaluate an expression. We propose a new algorithm for deriving such rigorous precision assignments and reducing the number of primitive computations needed. This algorithm can leverage results computed at lower precisions to analytically determine a precision for each primitive that will result in a sufficiently-accurate evaluation. It can also use information from constant subexpressions, movability flags, and repeat flags to skip the computation of certain primitives, further reducing the time to evaluate real expressions. Our implementation, Reval, achieves an average speed-up of 3.97x compared to the widely-used Sollya tool, with the speed-up increasing to 9.26x on the most difficult inputs. A detailed evaluation shows that this speed-up results from both assigning lower precisions to the majority of primitives and from computing fewer primitives overall.

papers.title: Almost Sure Convergence Rates and Concentration of Stochastic Approximation and Reinforcement Learning with Markovian Noise
papers.abstract: This paper establishes, to our knowledge, the first almost sure convergence rate and the first maximal concentration bound with sub-Weibull tails for general contractive stochastic approximation algorithms with Markovian noise. As a corollary, we also obtain convergence rates in $L^p$. Key to our successes is a novel discretization of the mean ODE of stochastic approximation algorithms using intervals with diminishing (instead of constant) length. Applications yield the first almost sure convergence rate for $Q$-learning without count-based learning rates and the first maximal concentration bound for off-policy temporal difference learning, both with Markovian samples.

papers.title: Stochastic Epidemic Models with Partial Information
papers.abstract: Mathematical models of epidemics often use compartmental models dividing the population into several compartments. Based on a microscopic setting describing the temporal evolution of the subpopulation sizes in the compartments by stochastic counting processes, one can derive macroscopic models for large populations describing the average behavior by associated ordinary differential equations as in the celebrated SIR model. Further, diffusion approximations allow one to address fluctuations from the average, which are also of interest in smaller populations, using stochastic differential equations. In general, not all state variables are directly observable, and we face the so-called "dark figure" problem, which concerns, for example, the unknown number of asymptomatic and unreported infections. The present study addresses this problem by developing partially observable stochastic epidemic models that account for uncertainty about the current state of the epidemic, also known as nowcast uncertainty. Examples include a simple extension of the SIR model, a model for a disease in which infection or vaccination confers lifelong immunity, and a Covid-19 model. For the latter, we propose a "cascade state approach" that allows us to exploit the information contained in formally hidden compartments with observable inflow but unobservable outflow. Furthermore, parameter estimation and calibration are performed using ridge regression for the Covid-19 model. The results of the numerical simulations illustrate the theoretical findings.

papers.title: The Cesàro Value Iteration
papers.abstract: In this paper, we consider undiscouted infinite-horizon optimal control for deterministic systems with an uncountable state and input space. We specifically address the case when the classic value iteration does not converge. For such systems, we use the Ces`aro mean to define the infinite-horizon optimal control problem and the corresponding infinite-horizon value function. Moreover, for this value function, we introduce the Cesàro value iteration and prove its convergence for the special case of systems with periodic optimal operating behavior. For this instance, we also show that the Cesàro value function recovers the undiscounted infinite-horizon optimal cost, if the latter is well-defined.
papers.comments: Extended version of "The Cesàro Value Iteration", IEEE Control Systems Letters, vol.9, pp.1934-1939, 2025 (DOI: 10.1109/LCSYS.2025.3584792)

papers.title: Emergent, spacetime-dependent dark energy and gravitational coupling from moving geometries
papers.abstract: We introduce the notion of moving Cartan geometries described by quotients of Lie groups and Lie algebras with spacetime dependant structure constants and construct associated deformed topological gauge action functionals for Lorentzian (including dS and AdS) and Lorentz$\times$Weyl moving geometries. The actions feature a generalization of the Nieh-Yan topological term for a varying coupling constant.
